"You joined <names>." waits for INSTANCE_INFO to name the stage group
(two seconds at most, then the slots' known names, else "You joined the
group."); a decision's notice without names says "the group" ("Joining the
group failed; you play this stage on your own."), never "Your friends is
...". The go-along notice goes once the player answered it: the own
request's line stands where it was (a *Cancel* brings it back while its
20 s run).

These texts are the port UI's: they stay English when the game text shows
another display language (main's F1 > Settings > Language, merged into the
integration on 2026-11-14; [L10N.md](L10N.md) 4: a language pack's
`[files] ui` is reserved for a later catalog of them). The area, stage and

### 19.6 Instance lifecycle

#### 19.6.1 Creation

A NEW decision for a fresh arrival (19.7) makes an instance:

- **Host:** always a member of the *base* group, the one whose load
  snapshot every co-arriving engine restores (3.4), because that snapshot
  holds the base's story and settings: the arriving member; for a
  co-arrival the base's first member; for a party the leader, whose group
  the relay makes the base (19.12). A host who is not the base would leave
  the base's story in every engine while the keeper is the host's (a story
  leak), so the relay never separates the two.
- **Visibility:** the prompt's choice, else `online_prefs.default_visibility`.
- **Settings:** the host's (19.8.7). **Story:** the host's keeper (19.8.1).
- **Area:** the area of the stage the host entered (19.30.2), fixed for
  the instance's life; that stage starts its visited set (19.30.3).
- A row of `instance_history` is queued (19.17.1).

BARRIER_OK tells every member of the arriving group the instance id, the
host's member id and the settings; INSTANCE_INFO follows.

#### 19.6.2 Visibility

- The host and staff change it at any time (INSTANCE_OP *visibility*), from
  the F1 Online tab's *Instance* page, which the line under the own status
  window opens with View (Q9's "status menu", 19.5.4).
- It applies to future prompts, browser rows, friend lists and co-arrivals.
  Members already inside stay. A travel or join already loading is checked
  again at its decision (19.9.4).
- The relay writes the host's choice back as his
  `online_prefs.default_visibility` through a queue (Q9: remembered).
- Audit row `instance_visibility` (19.17.1).

#### 19.6.3 Travel inside the instance (question 32)

- 3.4's decisions run among the instance's own stage groups: `Decide` and
  `JoinOrNew` (and the co-arrival search) take only stage groups of the
  arriving group's instance as candidates. A member never lands in another
  instance's stage group at a barrier inside its instance and is never
  prompted there; a NEW inside the instance is a new stage group of it and
  takes no seat.
- The exit port (5.2), the gate disc fork, *Give up*, story and boss mats
  (the original gather rule until round S3) and every other rule of 5 stay
  as built.
- A stage group without the host plays on the host's story. Its members'
  STORY goes to the host's keeper by the guest rules (19.8.1).
- When a stage group goes home (an exit into a hub stage, the gate disc, a
  game over, *Give up*), its guests are home; if the host is among them the
  instance ends (19.6.5), at once when he went on purpose, after his 60 s
  return when he was defeated (question 37). The side rule (6.7, "the dead
  travel with the living", `Engine::online_split`) stays as built: when the
  last living member of the host's stage group takes an exit home, a
  defeated host goes along, and that counts as defeated, not on purpose.
- *Go to Kim* (I3): a member's travel to another member (the host or any
  other) inside the instance, for one who wandered off; it never leaves
  the instance (GO, 19.9.6).
- **The area and the offer** (decision 38): every stage the members reach
  lies in the instance's area (19.30.2); a member who goes from a field
  into a dungeon makes the go-along offer to the members in fields
  (19.30.5), and *Go along* departs straight to the target inside the
  instance (GO, 19.30.7).

#### 19.6.4 A guest leaves

Through an exit into a hub stage, the gate disc, *Give up* while defeated
(its game over into its own lobby), *Leave instance* (INTENT kind 3 *leave*:
the relay stamps HOME for its slot), quitting (BYE, LEAVE), a removal
(19.6.6) or a connection lost beyond its seat (19.15). Its seat frees. Its
DISSOLVE replaces its story with its own (19.8.3).

#### 19.6.5 The end and HOME

An instance ends when:

- its host goes home on purpose: the host's own act brings his side to a
  barrier into a hub stage (an exit that leads into a hub stage, the gate
  disc, *Give up*), *Leave instance* (his INTENT *leave*), quitting or
  logging out (BYE), *Play* on another PC (CLOSE *replaced*, 19.17.3), a
  lock, ban or deletion of his account;
- its host was defeated (a game over of his stage group, or taken home
  along by the side rule) and does not return within
  `World:HostReturnSeconds` (60) (question 37's default; before round I3,
  whose travel the return needs, it ends at once);
- its host is not back within his grace (19.6.7);
- staff end it (19.14);
- its last member leaves;
- the server stops.

Q7's "exit" is read as an exit that leads home. An exit into another field,
dungeon or boss stage is travel inside the instance (19.6.3). Decision 38
says the same in the user's words: the instance ends when its host leaves
the area completely, and the only way out of an area is home (19.30.2,
the Fortress counting as Death Valley's). A dungeon's last exit after its
boss and a boss stage's exit lead into the lobby, so a host who takes
them ends the instance (19.30.1, fact 2).

**The defeated host's return** (question 37, round I3). His barrier into
the hub stage is held (BARRIER_WAIT reason *return*, `HoldKind.Return`)
before its transition steps, so his engine never runs his lobby while
guests play on his story (one writer per keeper); his seat is *held*;
guests see "Kim was defeated. Waiting for Kim... 52 s" and their story
values are held as in the grace (19.8.5). *A: Return* is a travel from the
parked barrier (19.9.2) next to the living guest with the most others
around it; *B*, the 60 s or no guest left: END `host_defeated`, his
DISSOLVE runs into his lobby. A *Give up* is on purpose (the player chose
it); only the game over and the side rule's pull are "defeated".

On the end the relay refuses joins and travels to the instance, sends
WORLD_NOTICE (*ended*, reason) and stamps **HOME(mask = every present slot,
reason)** in each of its stage groups at the first membership-safe tick at
least `World:EndNoticeTicks` (180, three seconds) ahead (6.5). In a solo-led
stage group HOME takes JOIN's path (6.6): JOIN_REQ with the kind *home*, the
leader answers with the tick (JOIN_AT) and the relay records the event in
the log there.

On every engine of the stage group the slots in the mask take the **home
departure**: the gate disc's records without SYSsetGateStage (SQ_EXIT for
those players, the fade, NEXTSTAGE stagML11 point 3). Every present slot in
the mask: the original group move; part of them: a fork of the new kind
`ForkKind::home`, in which **exactly the mask leaves, defeated or not**.
The gate disc's own fork cannot serve: `Engine::online_split`
(`online.cpp`, 6.7's side rule "the dead travel with the living") would
turn HOME for a defeated guest into no departure at all (no living leaver)
and HOME for the last living member into a move of every defeated one, the
host included. HOME is a server decision about accounts, so the side rule
does not apply to it. A stage group whose present slots are all defeated
after a HOME runs the original game over (that game over is "defeated" for
a host, 19.6.5; measured below). Its barrier is recognized by its alive
mask, not by its target: BARRIER carries `alive` (`Session::park`,
`session.cpp` 1259, `GameEngineLink::alive_mask`), and a barrier with no
living present slot is the game over whatever stage it names (measured
below: after a HOME it can name the field). **Except a Give up:** a
*Give up* (INTENT *give_up*, `Engine::online_intent`, `online.cpp`
541-547) forks the defeated member off alone, and that copy's game over
gives exactly such a barrier (alive mask 0, stagML11), but it is on
purpose (answers 24 and 37). The relay stamped the INTENT and the fork
lists name its side, so it knows the copy: a barrier with alive mask 0
counts as "defeated" only outside a give-up copy; in one it is the
member's own way home (a host's Give up ends his instance at once, a
guest's is his leave, 19.6.4). The barrier into stagML11 is
a DISSOLVE: every member home on its own story (19.8.3). A member's own window or talk closes as the gate
disc closes it. Members parked at a barrier get their DISSOLVE redirected
home (19.8.3); spectators go home.

**Measured r71 (corrected after the review): only defeated players after
a HOME.** `dw4_world_probe DATA homeover` (`tools/world_probe.cpp`,
headless, dng101b1 direct start with one to three players, online rules
unless "offline"): a defeat as in a fight (GAMERAM ADDHP 0 and SQ_DEAD, as
`tests/online_tests.cpp`'s *kill*), then HOME emulated in the copy that
keeps the other slots (`online_remove_player` per HOME slot: the despawn
and membership step the fork's other side gets, `online.cpp` 485-525).
Every stage change made pending is listed with the point and the alive
and present masks the BARRIER would carry (`GameEngineLink::alive_mask`,
`present_mask` and `pending_point`, read after the step that made it
pending, as `Session::park` reads them). The game over is the bit
capsule's: with no player model generated it runs `end_g_000bcaps.lua` on
every update (`ModelCtrlManager::update_capsule`, `model_ctrl.cpp`
2353-2377), and HOME's despawn removes the last living model
(`despawn_player` sends PLAYER REMOVE, `online.cpp` 492-497). The defeat
is ordered at the frame given (the kill), its SQ_ERAS ("player N
defeated") comes 72 frames later. Logs (worktree `i1ameas`)
`build/meas2/homeover_r2.log` with the script trace `homeover_r2.err`;
the script traces of single cases `ho_r1_c*.err`, `ho_r2_c*.err`; the
first runs `build/meas/homeover2.*`, `ho4_c2.*`, `ho_c*.err`, `ho_s*.log`.

| the same, HOME 10 frames after the kill (the death sequence still runs) | 1273 | 1211 | 1364 | 1464 **stag0101 2** (the exit prompt, below), alive 0 / present 2 |
| the same with the kill at 1800, HOME +10 / +300 | 1873 | 1811 / 2101 | 1964 / 2102 | 2366 / 2476 stagml11 0, alive 0 / present 2 |

So yes: a stage group left with only defeated players reaches the original
game over in online rules, one update after the HOME that removes the last
living model, or 91 frames after the last SQ_ERAS when HOME came during
the death sequence (as the game over without HOME: 1273 to 1364), and the
game over's NEXTSTAGE stagml11 follows 374-402 frames after the script,
as the original's offline (1364 to 1747, 383 frames, one and two players).
**Every one of these barriers has alive mask 0**, the exit prompt's too.

One case leaves elsewhere, and HOME causes it. In the second row the
defeated slot 1 lies on dng101b1's matz01 (the way back, which its pads
walked onto at 699) when HOME despawns the living slot 0 (1211); the copy
is solo, so the exit port is gone (`install_online_lua`: the port only
while two or more are present, `online_exits.cpp` 434-444); at 1275, as
slot 1's model goes, matz01's script runs and opens the stage change
prompt (i_zzstchgwb, 1276-1286), the defeated slot's pad answers it and
the NEXTSTAGE stag0101 point 2 follows at 1464, before the game over's own.
Without HOME the same two defeats on the same mat run the game over,
offline and in online rules alike (rows "both defeated": matz01's script
runs at 1276, gives control back without the prompt, and the game over
follows). The first runs read this as the original's rule for a solo
player who falls on an exit mat; measured, it is not: a solo player who
steps onto matz01 alive gets the prompt at once (last row), and the
prompt after a defeat comes only after HOME's despawn of the living
member. **Design change (r71):** the relay reads the game over from the
barrier's alive mask (0), not from its target stagML11, outside a give-up
copy (above): such a barrier is "defeated" for a host (question 37's
return in I3, the end before I3) and, when its instance has ended, it is
redirected home like every barrier of an ended instance (19.8.3).

HOME also serves a removal (one slot), a guest's *Leave instance* (its slot)
and a staff removal. EXP, items and Bits stay with every member; its
stage-change save (answer 3) uploads them.

#### 19.6.6 Removal (question 34)

INSTANCE_OP *remove* (the host or staff) stamps HOME for that member's slot.
The removed account cannot see or join that instance for
`World:RemovedBarMinutes` (10). It reads "You were removed from Kim's
instance."; staff removals are audited (`staff_remove`). A host who blocks a
guest removes it the same way (19.11).

**Binding on the server, whatever the client does.** At the removal the
relay at once: frees the seat; switches the removed member's story owner to
its own without waiting for a barrier (from then on a STORY with the host's
key is refused, reason *owner*, 19.8.4), so a modified client cannot keep
writing the host's story; and takes it out of the instance's lists. If its stage group
is solo-led and its client does not answer the *home* JOIN_REQ within
`Instances:JoinRequestTries`, the relay detaches that stage group from the
instance (a stage group of nobody's instance: no joins, no story, its next
barrier a DISSOLVE home with the redirect, 19.8.3). A member removed while it
waits at a barrier (gathering with its stage group, waiting for a JOIN or a
boss fight, or as the co-arrival of a holding base) goes home from that
barrier at once (a DISSOLVE redirected home, its own story) and never takes a
seat in the instance again while the bar lasts; the others decide on, and the
co-arrivals of a base left without members decide on their own (round I1b,
19.25).

Since fix-019 the relay also refuses (reason *owner*) every STORY from an
engine on another's story whatever owner key it names: a stage group of
nobody's instance, or of an instance the member holds no seat in (a
removed member; before, a STORY with the member's own key reached its own
keeper with the host's progress). A member removed **while it still
loads** (a JOIN not yet READY) gets no seat back when its JOIN falls back
(before, the fallback took a seat past the removal bar and the four
seats): its fallback NEW is a stage group of nobody's instance with HOME
at once, asked again like an instance's, and its way home is the DISSOLVE
with the replace; the same when the instance went meanwhile (before, the
fallback made an own instance whose merge carried the former host's
story into the own). An instance that goes with its last seat detaches
the stage groups it leaves behind (removed members still playing in
them), so their next barrier goes home too instead of being a fresh
arrival.

The refix of fix-019 (the review of fix-019): **a JOIN never takes a
seat.** A fresh arrival removed while it waits for its automatic JOIN (an
entry scene's hold of up to `Instances:JoinHoldSeconds`, a boss choice)
leaves the wait at once and decides again on its own, where the bar
counts: another instance or its own (before, in 0.1.8 too, the JOIN at the
hold's end took the seat back past the bar and the four seats, "joined"
went to everyone again with a second history row, and an arrival that had
taken the freed seat meanwhile was pushed into an instance of its own). A
member removed at its stage group's barrier joins without a seat and goes
home from the target's stage group by its owed HOME, as from a NEW. A
detached stage group's former host plays his own story there, so his
STORY still reaches his keeper (19.8.5). Until its way home, an engine on
another's story without a seat there (a removed member, a fallback from
nobody's instance, a JOIN whose seat went) is that instance's guest in the
achievements' play context (19.8.9). W10s checks the fallback from
nobody's instance with a real client (a staff removal during a classic
catch-up whose target leaves the stage).

#### 19.6.7 The host's connection loss (Q8)

- **When it starts.** Today the relay notices a lost connection in two
  ways that do not fit Q8: `HousekeepInstance` (`RoomHub.cs`, "Lag and
  disconnects") stamps a LEAVE (`lagOut`) after `Relay:LagLeaveSeconds`
  (10) of filling while the connection still counts as open, and
  `RelayHub`'s housekeeping closes a silent connection only after
  `Relay:IdleTimeoutSeconds` (60). A half-open connection (Wi-Fi gone, a NAT
  timeout: no FIN, no RST) would make the host vanish after 10 s, and the
  grace would start only after 60 s (up to 120 s in all). So the grace
  starts at the **first** of: the close, or `World:HostSilenceSeconds` (4)
  without INPUT and PONG from the host while his slot fills. While the host
  is in his grace, `lagOut` does not apply to his slot, and the idle
  timeout ends nothing early: the grace's deadline decides.
- **During the grace.** The host's slot is filled with neutral pads from
  the first missing tick on (not "last pad, then neutral" as for a guest, so
  his Digimon stands still; it can be hit) until `World:HostGraceSeconds`
  (60) after the start instead of `Relay:ReconnectSeconds` (10, which stays
  for guests). The host's RESUME window is at least the grace:
  `Instances:MaxResumeTicks` rises to 4,200 for a host (60 s at 59.94 Hz
  plus 600), or round J's checkpoint resume covers it. Guests see the
  countdown; rows read *Host reconnecting*; joins and travels wait; guests'
  story values are held (19.8.5). The world's member timeout
  (`World:MemberTimeoutSeconds`, 35, as the room's) does not apply to a host
  in his grace: he stays a world member until the grace's end plus
  `World:MemberTimeoutMarginSeconds` (10).
- **A solo-led host stage group** plays on in the host's client until its
  barrier (6.10); the relay counts the grace all the same.
- **Back in time:** RESUME, "Kim is back." His slot's fill streak counts
  for `lagOut` from his return, not from the grace's start: his client has
  `Relay:LagLeaveSeconds` to catch up to the ticks sealed meanwhile and then
  plays on in his stage group (round I1b's fix stage after the merge of main:
  before, a host away longer than that was taken out by `lag_leave` a quarter
  second after `host_back`). A return past the grace's deadline, before the
  housekeeping's next pass ended the instance, is not in time.
- **A link that keeps dropping** ("flapping": closes or silences again and
  again; fix-flap). Two rules bound it:
  - *One grace per absence episode.* A drop less than
    `Relay:LagLeaveSeconds` after his last return belongs to the same
    episode: its grace keeps the deadline of the episode's first grace,
    whose countdown runs on while he is briefly back (the guests' notice
    shows the seconds left, not 60; `host_grace_continued`); a deadline
    already past ends the instance at the next housekeeping (`host_lost`, as
    any grace's end). Back for `Relay:LagLeaveSeconds`, a later drop is a
    new loss with a fresh grace; two losses closer than that count as one
    (the second gets what the first left of its 60 s: W7's run of fix-flap
    had a 5 ms silence grace, a stall of the client, 10.09 s before its
    cut, which so got a fresh grace; 0.1 s earlier it would have had 50 s,
    still enough for the 20 s cut).
  - *One restart of the lag clock per fill streak* (6.4: the ticks filled
    since a pad of his was last sealed in time). His first return in the
    streak restarts it as above; a further return only moves it on by that
    absence, so `lagOut` counts his connected time since his first return,
    `Relay:LagLeaveSeconds` in all.

  **The bound:** from the first filled tick of his slot he is out of the
  guests' stage group (`lag_leave`: he plays apart, still host, the
  instance goes on) or his instance has ended (`host_lost`) within
  `Relay:LagLeaveSeconds` (lagging before his first drop) +
  `World:HostGraceSeconds` (the episode's deadline) +
  `Relay:LagLeaveSeconds` (back at that deadline: a further drop within it
  ends the instance, connected that long with late pads the lag rule takes
  him out), 80 s with the defaults plus the housekeeping's quarter seconds:
  the worst case of one absence (lagging 9.9 s, closed, back after 59.9 s,
  10 s to catch up), so the guests never play against his standing Digimon
  longer than one absence could make them, unless he comes back for
  `Relay:LagLeaveSeconds` with his pads in time (then he plays); outside
  `lagOut`'s own exceptions (everyone lags, a resync). The episode rule is
  the one that holds the real client: its pads are made on the wall clock,
  so the pads of its last ticks before each return arrive in time and end
  the fill streak every time (W7g's first run, on a rule of the fill streak
  alone: a fresh grace at every cut, for good). A host who does not catch
  up between brief drops (his pads late, no such burst) is taken out by the
  lag rule first, the instance going on. Before, every return restarted the
  clock, every drop started a fresh grace, and 4 s of silence start a grace
  before 10 s of lag count: such a host stayed in his stage group for good.
  A host outside a sealed stage group (lone after `lag_leave`, solo-led)
  has no guest in his group; his graces follow the same episode rule. A
  flapping **guest** is not on this path: no grace, and his reconnects never
  restart his slot's clock, so `lagOut` takes him out
  `Relay:LagLeaveSeconds` after his streak's first fill however his link
  comes and goes (`Relay:ReconnectSeconds` counts each drop on its own);
  with his pads in time between the drops he plays on, as before. No
  setting of its own: the rule uses the grace's and the lag rule's keys
  (`WorldFlapTests`, W7g).
- **A crash** (the engine lost): within the grace only with round I5 (a
  checkpoint rejoin of his own slot, 19.15); before I5 a crashed host ends
  his instance after 60 s.
- **At a barrier.** Guests never wait for a lost host on their loading
  screens (Q8: "the instance runs on"): the barrier is decided without him,
  as `Disconnect` decides it today, and the stage group goes on to its
  target; the host keeps his seat and his grace. Back within the grace, his
  client, still parked at that barrier (today's `Connect` would mark him
  lone at a `Barrier` / `Arrival` and his client would go on as NEW after
  5 s), is resumed into it: he arrives alone and JOINs his own instance's
  stage group at the target (3.4's hold, no prompt; classic before round J,
  from a checkpoint after it). Not back: his parked barrier becomes a
  DISSOLVE home when he reconnects (19.6.10).
- **Not back:** END `host_lost`, HOME for everyone.
- **The test** W7 runs with a proxy that cuts by closing the connection and
  W7c with one that swallows packets without FIN or RST; W7d holds a
  reconnect at 45 s to prove the member timeout does not end the grace; W7g
  swallows them for 7 s at a time, 0.2 s apart (a flapping link): one
  episode's countdown, `host_lost` at its deadline, inside the bound.

#### 19.6.8 Desync

6.9 is unchanged inside the instance: a member that cannot be repaired in
time continues alone as a new stage group of the same instance, on the
host's story, with its seat (free travel allows a stage group of one). Its
STORY counts by its role.

#### 19.6.9 Events at a glance

| Event | Server | Engines | Players see |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| A member takes an exit to another field | barrier inside the instance (3.4 filtered) | 5.2 as built | "Lee went to B2." |
| A member goes from a field into a dungeon | barrier inside the instance; the go-along offer to the members in fields (19.30.5) | 5.2 as built | "Kim went into Ancient Ruins B1. Go along?  View: answer" |
| A member goes along | INTENT 4 held until the entrants' floor is joinable, then GO stamped; its barrier joins the entrants at the entrance (19.30.7) | the exit port's departure for the GO slots of one step (`ForkKind::go`: the exit's side rule, forked between two steps) | "Going along when Kim's floor is ready..."; "Joining Kim..."; "Lee joined." |
| A guest goes home (exit into a hub, gate disc, game over) | DISSOLVE, seat freed | as built | "Lee left." |
| A guest's *Leave instance* | HOME(slot) | home departure (fork) | "Lee left." |
| The host goes home on purpose | END `host_left`, HOME(all) after 3 s | home departure | "Kim left. The instance ends." |
| The host's connection lost | grace 60 s, neutral pads | the host's Digimon stands | countdown |
| Grace over | END `host_lost`, HOME(all) | home departure | "Kim did not come back. The instance ends." |
| The host is defeated (game over, or the side rule) | I3: return hold 60 s; before I3: END `host_defeated` | the host parked before his lobby; the guests play on | "Kim was defeated. Waiting for Kim..." |
| Removal | HOME(slot), bar 10 min, owner switched at once | home departure (`ForkKind::home`) | "You were removed..." |
| Staff end | END `staff`, HOME(all), audit | home departure | "A moderator ended this instance." |
| Server stop (planned) | "Server restart in 60 s." (19.26 idea 7), then CLOSE `stopping` | the session ends; the engine in a field takes the home departure itself | "The server restarted. Back on your own story." |
| Server crash or kill | nothing; the new process knows no instance | WELCOME without an instance: the home departure itself (19.6.10) | the same |

#### 19.6.10 Lost instances: the local way home

An engine can end up in a field whose instance the relay no longer knows:
the server restarted or crashed (the new process has no instances, and
clients reconnect to it), the instance ended while the client was away
beyond its resume window, a host came back after his grace, a removed
client ignored its *home* JOIN_REQ. In every such case the client takes the
home departure **itself**: `Engine::online_depart_home()` (19.9.2) is
allowed for any solo engine whose instance the relay does not know (WELCOME
or RESUME without the instance, or WORLD_NOTICE *ended* for it), for every
member, not only at home. Nothing else replays that engine (no relay
instance holds it, so nobody can join or log it), so the local departure
is as safe as at home. Its barrier into stagML11 is a DISSOLVE with the
replace (19.8.3) and the own story from WELCOME; "The server restarted.
Back on your own story." or "The instance has ended." EXP, items and Bits
stay (the stage-change upload runs as usual). Values the field made on the
host's story after the last STORY_ACK are lost for the host (his keeper
never saw them); his own are queued as always (19.8.4). Scenarios W24
(an ordered restart) and W25 (the server process killed) check it with a
guest and a host in a field: both home on their own stories, `online_card.dat`
and the server revisions unchanged by the foreign story.

### 19.7 Arrivals: matching and the prompt

#### 19.7.1 When

At the departure of a *fresh arrival* into a joinable stage (not
`StageNames.IsHub`): a group from home. Never for a group already in an
instance (it travels inside its instance and its area; since round 72 a host
alone in his instance too, 19.30.3, decision 41), a party member arriving
with its leader (I4), a travel, a seat rejoin.

- A *starting* instance (19.3, 19.7.6) at that stage that the arrival may
  see and that has seats for it: co-arrival without a prompt (answer 21).
- Else candidates exist in the stage's area (19.7.2, 19.30.3): the prompt,
  in the gate form (19.7.4) or the loading-screen form (19.7.5).
- Nothing: NEW with the remembered visibility, the toast.

Round I1a builds the world without the prompt: there an arrival from home
with candidates enters automatically the row the prompt would preselect
(19.7.3, decision 40), a JOIN at the stage or as a guest in a new stage
group there (19.30.4), with the toast "You joined Kim's instance. Kim is
in <stage>. Leave: Online menu"; where the prompt would preselect *New
instance*, it makes a new instance (`Matching.AutoJoinRow` =
`Preselected`).

**The I1a interim rule** (fix-019, the review of 0.1.7: I1a went live as
0.1.7 and 0.1.8 without I1b, against "never deployed without I1b"): the
automatic join takes only a first row that is not greyed and is the
party's (I4) or a friend's (the host a friend, or friends in it) or has
players of its instance at the arrival stage; otherwise *New instance*.
Before it, I1a took the first non-greyed row, also a stranger's instance
with nobody of it at the arrival stage, which made a quick player a guest
in a stranger's story elsewhere in the area. The guest's NEW (19.30.4)
stays I1a's to test with a friend (W30, W30x, W6 make a and b friends;
W29's fake guests befriend the host). Round I1b's prompt replaces the
automatic join; staff pass the visibility only by their own choice of a
row (19.7.2), never in the automatic join.

(Before round 72 a host alone in his instance who moved on was a fresh
arrival too, with *Join* ending his instance and *Continue alone* keeping
it. With instances per area his moves stay inside his instance and are
never prompted, 19.30.3; the user confirmed it on 2026-11-06, decision
41.)

#### 19.7.2 Who sees what: Visible() and the candidates

**Visible(instance i, member m)** is true when all of these hold:

- no block in either direction between m and any member of i;
- m is not under a removal bar of i;
- i is Public; or i is Friends and m is a friend of i's host or in the
  host's party; or i is Private and m is in the host's party; or m is staff
  and chooses the row himself (wish (a): staff join "no matter how the
  instance was set": a prompt row, I1b, or the browser, I3). The automatic
  join and the co-arrivals (19.7.6) are no choice of his: there a
  moderator who simply plays is a player for the visibility too (fix-019;
  before, I1a put him into strangers' Private and Friends instances and
  replaced his story with theirs). `Matching.Visible(..., staffChoice)`.
  In 0.1.9 (I1a: no prompt, no browser) no code path passes the staff
  choice yet, so a moderator who simply plays enters a Private or Friends
  instance only as the host's friend (from I4 also in his party); W18 runs
  on a Public instance. I1b's prompt passes it for its rows, and its
  preselection never takes a row that only the staff bypass shows.

For staff the first two give way only to an explicit moderation action:
*Spectate*, *Join as moderator* (a staff row's second action, audited
`staff_join_override`), *End* and *Remove*. A moderator who simply plays is
a player for blocks and bars: a griefer cannot block every moderator out,
and a player who blocked a moderator is not followed by him into instances
without a logged reason.

The relay recomputes it at every OPTIONS, BROWSE, friend list update and
decision, from its social cache (19.17.2), and never trusts a client's list.

**Candidates of an arrival at stage S with context hash C** (3.7; round 72:
per area, 19.30.3): the instances of S's area visible to every member of
the arriving group, with context C and the arrival's data hash (19.17.3),
not ending, and listed with their state:

- joinable now, with seats for the whole group: a JOIN at S when the
  instance has a stage group there, else entering as a guest in a new
  stage group at S (19.30.4) when S is a gate stage whose gate the host's
  story has opened, or visited;
- *Story not here yet* (greyed): no stage group at S, and S is neither a
  gate stage whose gate the host's story has opened nor visited (19.30.3);
  choosable from round I3 by *Join at <host>*;
- *Boss fight* (boss-locked): choosing it waits (19.7.7);
- *Host reconnecting* (greyed, not choosable);
- *Full* (greyed; for staff *Spectate*, I3);
- *Arriving now*: no stage group at S, but one of the instance at a barrier
  for S, or its members parked on their way there (decision 46, built in
  round I1b's integration): choosable, the arrival waits for their stage
  group at S and joins it (`Instances:JoinHoldSeconds` at most, then a
  NEW with 3.4's hold-expired notice, as a JOIN's hold); never
  preselected, never the automatic join; its players are not *Here*;
- before round J, beyond `Instances:MaxCatchUpSeconds`: "Too long to catch
  up" (greyed); after J the check goes;
- *Other settings* (greyed) only for a setting I1a's first task finds
  unswitchable (19.8.7).

Plus, at the top, the own party's instance wherever it is (I4), as a travel
row ("Join your party (Kim): Cliff Dungeon B3"). At most 8 rows, then *New
instance* always last.

The states *Boss fight*, *Arriving now* and *Too long to catch up* are
those of the instance's stage group at S. The prompt lists the instances
of the arrival's area (decision 38; until round 72 only those with a stage
group at the target stage, with 19.26 idea 17's area rows as a proposal):
a player who takes the gate to Dry Land while Kim's instance is in Ancient
Ruins B2 gets Kim's row ("Ancient Ruins B2") and enters as a guest where
he walked in (19.30.3, 19.30.4); from round I3 the row's *Y: Join at Kim*
travels next to Kim (19.9). Decision 40 (the user's answer of
2026-11-06): such rows rank after those with players at the arrival stage
and are never preselected over *New instance* unless they are the party's
or a friend's (19.7.3); *A* on them still enters where he walked in.

#### 19.7.3 Order and preselection (Q13, decision 40)

Q13's order: "party and friends first, then the best ping and free slots".
Decision 40 (the user's answer of 2026-11-06, "Spieler vor Ort zuerst",
"players on the spot first") puts the instances with players at the
arrival stage right after party and friends: Q13's ping and free seats
then order within the rows with players there and, after them, within the
rows with nobody there (the grouping is step 3's, not the ping's).

1. the own party's instance;
2. friends: the host a friend, then the most friends inside;
3. players of the instance at the arrival's stage (decision 40, 19.30.3; a
   badge "Here (n)" on the row): rows with any before rows with none;
4. joinable now, by ping (the highest round-trip median among the
   instance's members, the relay's `RttSamples`, lowest first; pings within
   10 ms of each other count as equal);
5. more free seats for the arriving group;
6. more of the instance's players at the arrival's stage (round 72);
7. the same story point as the arriving player's own (19.8.6; from round
   I2), only as the last tie-breaker; it is a badge on the row ("Same story
   point"), so a player who wants it sees it;
8. the older instance.

Greyed and waiting rows (boss fight, host reconnecting, full, story not here yet)
come after all joinable ones, also after those with nobody at the arrival
stage. A stage group at the arrival stage that is joinable in a moment (a
scene, its loading: state *loading*, 3.4's JOIN waits for it) is no such
row: it keeps its place in steps 1-3 and follows the rows joinable now
within step 4 (round I1b's review: a friend's instance in a short scene
fell behind a stranger's row, which took the cursor). The first row is preselected when it is not greyed and is the
party's (step 1) or a friend's (step 2: the host a friend or friends in
it) or has players of its instance at the arrival stage; otherwise *New
instance* is (decision 40). Only the first row decides: the cursor never
skips to a later row. So a row with nobody of its instance at the arrival
stage is never preselected unless it is the party's or a friend's, and a
quick A never makes a player a guest in a stranger's story elsewhere in
the area. Such a row is still listed and chosen with A (the player enters
where he walked in, 19.30.4; from round I3 its *Y: Join at <host>*
travels next to the host). The relay sends
OPTIONS again on a change, at most once a second, with the preselection
decided again. The client keeps the cursor the player moved on the same
instance (or on *New instance*); a cursor he has not moved takes the
refreshed preselection, so the rule above holds through a refresh too (round
I1b's second review: a row whose players left the arrival stage lost its
claim, and a quick A on the kept cursor made the player a guest of a
stranger elsewhere). The prompt's line about a chosen instance ("Kim's
instance is full now.") stays through refreshes while no row of that host
can be chosen, and goes once one can.

*Players of the instance at the arrival's stage* (steps 3 and 6, the
preselection; fix-019's refix) are the members of its stage groups that
stay at that stage (no barrier, not an exit fork's leaving side, not past
their log's end: the stage groups a JOIN could take) and their joiners.
Never the members of a stage group at a barrier to another stage (before,
they counted while their group waited at the exit, so the row became a
preselected guest's NEW and I1a's interim rule put a stranger alone into a
new stage group of their instance), nor a member playing on alone at the
stage (another engine: the arrival would not meet it either). A stage
group at a barrier *for* the arrival's stage is I1b's *Arriving now*
(decision 46): it ranks with the boss fights, after every row that can be
entered now or in a moment, and is never preselected, so decision 40's
preselection of the other rows stays as it was.

#### 19.7.4 The gate form (Q13: standing at the gate)

- **Census first** (round I1b's first task): every departure from a hub
  stage into a joinable stage, from the decompiled scripts: the lobby gate's
  destination select (`stagML11_m1__mate00.lua`), the quest boards' starts
  (`stagML11_m1__quest01..04.lua`), the return mat (`mate02.lua`), the
  briefing room's and the event console's starts. For each, whether a
  read-only engine accessor `Engine::pending_departure_choice()` can name
  the stage and point that the own player's next confirming press would
  start (for mate00: the SELECTCTRL cursor and its DMcase's NEXTSTAGE). The
  departures it can name get the gate form, the rest the loading-screen
  form.

  *Measured (round I1b, prompt lane, 2026-11-07).* The census of the
  decompiled scripts finds two such departures, and the accessor names
  both: stagML11 `mate00` (the lobby gate, SELECTCTRL `i_zzstchgcur`, one
  DMcase per area with SETGENERATEPOS and NEXTSTAGE) and stagML11 `mate02`
  (the return mat, `i_zzstchgwn`, *Yes* = DMcase 0 to SYSgetGateStage's
  stage and point). The quest boards (`quest01..04`) only set flags (409,
  376-381 ...); the same gate menu then offers one line, stag0401 point 3,
  so a quest's start is the gate's departure. The briefing room (stagML02:
  its mat and gate disc lead to stagML11), the event console (stagML12 to
  stagML02), the shops and the stagIS* stages lead only into hub or UI
  stages: no arrival, no prompt. `data/online/stage_graph.json` has no
  static edge from a hub stage into a field (`PromptTests`). `dw4_world_probe
  DATA census` (headless, online rules, the player put onto the mat, the
  menu opened by the stage's own script) read the accessor at every line of
  the gate's menu (training, after the training, phases 5 and 6, a quest's
  start) and of the return mat's (two Security Gate stages), then pressed
  A: 12 of 12 named destinations equal the stage and point the press
  started (224 frames from the press to NEXTSTAGE at the gate, 211 at the
  mat), and the mat's *No* line names nothing and starts nothing; B on the
  gate's menu starts nothing and the accessor names nothing afterwards.
  So every hub departure into a field gets the gate form; the
  loading-screen form serves a lost PLAN (no OPTIONS within
  `World:PlanWaitMs`), a departure posted outside a menu (the development
  build's `depart` action) and the test hook `DW4_ONLINE_TEST_GATE_FORM=0`
  (W11b). Log: `build/i1bp/meas/census_r3.log` (worktree `i1b-prompt`).
  The lobby's point next to each departure (19.7.5's *Back to the lobby*),
  from `dw4_world_probe DATA mats stagml11` (the mats and the generate
  points): the gate (mate00, x -5..15, z -105..-85) has point 1 at (0, -40)
  nearest, the return mat (mate02, x 145..165, z 45..65) point 3 at
  (210, 120) (points 2 (60, 20) and 4 (250, 70) are farther; point 0 and
  every undefined one are (60, -30)); the accessor names them
  (`DepartureChoice::back_point`).
- **The hold.** When the own player's press would confirm such a choice,
  the client keeps that press out of the pad stream (the engine sees neutral
  pads), sends PLAN and waits for OPTIONS (one round trip, well under 100 ms
  on the user's server). No candidate, or only an automatic co-arrival: the
  press goes out at once, one round trip after it was made. Otherwise the
  overlay opens.
- **It never sticks.** No OPTIONS within `World:PlanWaitMs` (1,000): the
  press goes out anyway and the departure runs; its barrier is then decided
  as a loading-screen arrival (19.7.5), so a lost answer costs the gate
  form, never the press. The connection lost while the overlay is open: the
  overlay closes, the held press is dropped (the player stands at the gate
  as after B) and "Connection lost. Try the gate again in a moment." shows.
  PLAN is throttled like BROWSE: at most one a second per member; a second
  confirm within that second waits for the first answer. (The client spaces
  its PLANs a second apart by its own clock; the relay takes them 900 ms
  apart by their arrival, so the network's jitter never drops a regular
  second try.)
- **The answer.** *A* on an instance or *New instance*: the held press goes
  out in the next pad, and the CHOICE travels with the departure's HEADING
  and BARRIER. A travel row (the party's instance elsewhere): a B press goes
  to the game (the menu closes), then the travel (19.9). *B*: a B press goes
  to the game; the original cancel closes the destination menu, and the
  player stands at the gate.
- **Why it is safe.** The lobby is a solo hub instance: never joined, it
  sends no LOG (3.3, 6.3). The simulation sees an A press later, the same in
  every replay; no barrier, hold or park depends on a person, and nothing in
  the engine waits on the network.

#### 19.7.5 The loading-screen form

Every other fresh arrival (a quest board's start if the census cannot name
it, the return mat's arrival if it cannot, any departure the census
missed): the relay holds its barrier (`HoldKind.Prompt`, BARRIER_WAIT reason
*choice* with OPTIONS) without a time limit. Only its own loading screen
waits: the arriving group is alone (from home). The
client's five-second "no answer, go on as NEW" rule (3.4) does not fire
while it shows the prompt. *A*: JOIN or NEW with the visibility.

*B* keeps Q13's "B leaves the player standing at the gate" as far as a
loading screen can:

- **A departure from home:** B is *Back to the lobby*: the DISSOLVE
  redirect of 19.8.3 back to the hub stage it left, at the point next to
  the departure it took (the census of 19.7.4 names it; stagML11 point 3
  when it names none). A reload of the lobby, on the own story; nothing of
  the field was played.
- Since round 72 every fresh arrival comes from home (19.30.3), so B is
  always *Back to the lobby*; the lone host's *Continue alone* went with
  his prompt (decision 41: he is never asked).

**The connection lost meanwhile.** The relay forgets the hold at a
disconnect (`DetachLocked` drops `m.Arrival`), so a prompt shown after it
would answer nobody: the client closes the prompt at the loss and 3.4's
rule applies (RESUME within the window re-sends the BARRIER, which is
decided anew, possibly with a new prompt; else after 5 s the client goes on
as NEW, a new instance that the relay files when the session is back).

#### 19.7.6 Co-arrival (answer 21)

3.4's timing is unchanged (HEADING, `Instances:CoArrivalHoldMs` 3,000, the
later groups spawned in the base's load step). In the world:

- **Automatic** only among fresh arrivals whose base *starts a new
  instance*: the later groups become guests of the base's host if the new
  instance is visible to them (staff without the bypass: a co-arrival is
  automatic, 19.7.2) and has seats for them. Toast: "You arrived
  together with Kim: you're a guest in Kim's story. Leave: Online menu."
- A base holds only for announced groups that may see it and did not
  choose a row in a prompt. A member who chose *New instance* lands with
  the others leaving with it (decision 43, 2026-11-11): it is the co-arrival
  of a base it may see (the same rules: visibility, blocks, bars), a base
  holds for it, and one a moment late joins the base's *starting* instance
  like any arrival (below), unless that instance was a row of its own
  prompt that it passed over (then it gets its own new instance). A member
  who chose a row joins its row and is nobody's base or co-arrival.
- **The window is ten seconds, not one.** `Decide` (`RoomHub.cs`) holds a
  base only for groups whose HEADING was already there at its barrier, and
  HEADING is sent at the fade's start (`Engine::note_departure`), so the
  real co-arrival window is one or two seconds. In a room today the
  automatic JOIN with its 30 s hold (`JoinOrNew`, `HoldKind.Join`) catches
  the rest; in the world a player 2-8 s behind A would find A's new
  instance running and get the prompt, against answer 21. So a new instance
  counts as *starting* (19.3) until its stage group is first joinable or
  `World:StartingSeconds` (10) after its NEW: a later fresh arrival that may
  see it and fits JOINs it without a prompt, at the entrance with 3.4's
  hold, as a co-arrival does (the same toast). After that window the
  prompt rules apply. W4b checks B 6 s after A.
- The arriving group of a running instance (members moving inside it) is
  never an automatic base for others: it is a prompt row *Arriving now*
  (answer 21: a foreign instance already runs).
- Parties co-arrive with their leader whatever the visibility, and the
  leader's group is always their base (19.6.1, 19.12).

#### 19.7.7 The choice and the races

CHOICE is checked again at the decision:

- **Join:** JOIN at the entrance point the arrival came through (3.4), with
  3.4's hold until joinable; where the instance has no stage group at the
  stage (round 72), a NEW as a guest: a new stage group of the instance
  with the host's story by the replace (19.30.4).
- **Boss-locked:** BARRIER_WAIT's existing *Wait for <names>* (JOIN when the
  lock clears) or *Go alone*: a new instance of the arrival's own, on its
  own story, with the visibility last chosen, as before round 72. Never a
  new stage group of the chosen instance at that stage: that would be a
  second copy of the host's boss fight, which the arrival could win alone
  in the host's story.
- **Full, ended, no longer visible meanwhile:** a refreshed prompt with the
  line "Kim's instance is full now." (gate form: before the departure;
  loading-screen form: the barrier keeps waiting).
- **New:** NEW with the visibility; a base for automatic co-arrivals,
  and itself the co-arrival of another base it may see or of a starting
  instance it was not offered (decision 43, 19.7.6).

### 19.8 Story only in the field

#### 19.8.1 Keepers

`RoomStoryKeeper` becomes `StoryKeeper`, one per (account, box) in the hub's
registry: created when the account enters the world (the bound box's story;
box 1 until round D), saved through `OnlineStoryService`'s queue as today
(history, revisions, round 59's session rows), dropped some minutes after
the account left the world and its instances ended. Exactly one keeper and
one writer per (account, box).

An instance's story is its host's keeper:

- **Owner rules** for the host's own STORY: per visit (8.7), not spaced
  (round 59's owner exemption), the earned queue.
- **Guest rules** for a guest's STORY in the host's instance: round 59's
  spacing per account (phase steps 300 s, key items 60 s, flags 8 at once
  then one per 30 s), the session growth caps, the earned queue, round G's
  key setter stages.

Mirrored progress (19.8.6) goes through the guest's own keeper.

**A story replaced from outside.** Today `RoomService.CloseOwnedAsync`
runs at the player's story reset (`OnlineCharacterEndpoints.cs`), the
admin's reset and the admin's story restore (`AdminEndpoints.cs`, the web's
`Admin/Account`), because "the hub holds the old story and would save it
again". A live keeper per (account, box) has the same problem, so these
paths call `IWorldNotifier.StoryReplaced(account, box)` (through
`WorldService`, 19.17.2). The relay then, under its lock: refuses the
keeper's merges and mirrors from that moment (a `replacing` flag), ends an
instance the account hosts on that box (END `staff` for an admin action,
`host_left` for the player's own reset, which only runs at the title
anyway), reloads the keeper from the database after the service's write
commits (the notifier's second call `StoryReplaced(..., done)`), and sends
the account's session a STORY_ACK with the new revision; a client at home
gets the new story at its next DISSOLVE or Game Start, as with an admin
edit today. Scenario W28 resets and restores a story while its player is
in the world.

#### 19.8.2 Which story an engine holds

| Moment | Story in the engine | How |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Game Start online | the own (bound box) | the title's application (8.5) with the own confirmed story from WELCOME; round G's hold reads "Loading your story..." |
| Own lobby, every hub stage | the own | the title, or the replace at DISSOLVE (19.8.3) |
| NEW from home (the host) | the own = the instance's | the barrier's merge, as today |
| NEW from home as a guest (an area instance without a stage group at the arrival stage, round 72) | the host's | the replace at the load step with the host's story, the host's modes and cheats at BARRIER_OK before the module reload (19.30.4) |
| JOIN, co-arrival, travel into an instance | the host's | the restore of the target's snapshot or checkpoint, as today |
| A barrier inside the instance (a GO's too) | the host's | the merge of the host keeper's confirmed story (8.5) |
| Back home (gate disc, exit into a hub, HOME, game over) | the own | **replace** (19.8.3); the host's own needs none |
| Spectator | the host's | observer; leaving restores the own lobby (19.14) |

#### 19.8.3 The return home (a new engine path)

- **What BARRIER_OK carries.** For a DISSOLVE, each member's own story: its
  keeper's newest revision rebased onto its own difficulty (working set and
  copies, as `StoryMerge.Rebase` does today), its own settings (19.8.7) and
  the story mode *replace*; for the host, whose engine story is his own, the
  mode *merge*. For a guest that is not in step whose barrier leads into a
  hub stage other than stagML11 (the host's briefing room, stagML02), a
  redirect to stagML11 point 3: the briefing's scripts would otherwise run
  on the guest's own story at a point its story never reached. In round I1
  every guest counts as not in step (the census class `mainline` and the
  story point come with round I2), so I1 redirects every guest whose
  barrier leads into stagML02.
- **The order at a barrier into a hub stage** (a boss's end into stagML02,
  for example): first the STORY of every member (as every barrier sends
  STORY first, 6.3), then the host keeper's merge, then the mirror
  (19.8.6), and only then the in-step test and each member's replace
  payload. A payload computed before the mirror would land an in-step
  guest in stagML02 without the boss's clear, in front of the briefing
  before the boss. The payload holds the own keeper's confirmed revision
  plus the values the mirror queued for it (the earned queue or
  `MinVisitSeconds` may hold a mirrored value back); the client keeps them
  as pending of its own story (19.8.4), as the host's engine keeps its own.
- **The load step.** After the existing DISSOLVE steps (the others
  despawned, the own player to slot 0, the personal values written back,
  3.7) and before the hub's load scripts: the story subset is replaced
  completely with the own (phase one-hot, the persistent flags with 503, the
  difficulty copies, K0-K10, COUNTER 1 and 7); the session context values
  the guest set aside at its join come back (19.8.8); the modes (difficulty,
  camera, light) and the engine settings (randomizer, fast loading) are set
  to its own. `start.lua` then lays out the lobby by the own phase. The
  engine is solo after the dissolve, so this is deterministic. The maps are
  written directly (no `story_flag` port event), so a replace gives no
  achievement.
- **The redirect** (`Engine::redirect_pending_stage(stage, point)`) is
  allowed only for a solo engine parked at a DISSOLVE, before its transition
  steps; it replaces `pending_stage_` (consumed in `begin_stage_load`,
  `engine.cpp` around 723-725; the step's load at about 2038-2041 after
  `apply_barrier`; the reload check at about 1970) and the arrival point,
  which the original passes on as PLAYERPOINT SETGENERATEPOS (the
  departure records read at about 572): the redirect replaces that generate
  point too, or the player would spawn at the old stage's point number in
  the new stage. Round I1a's first task proves that a redirect gives the same
  state as a NEXTSTAGE to that stage and point (the load step's snapshot
  hash). Its uses: the not-in-step guest above, members parked at a barrier
  when their instance ends, a returning host whose grace ran out (19.6.7),
  a defeated host's *End* when his barrier led elsewhere than stagML11
  (19.6.5), and B in the loading-screen form from home (19.7.5).
- **Measured r71 (extended after the review): the redirect against a NEXTSTAGE.** The stage change's
  path, with the places a redirect could go:
  1. *Lua.* The original's NEXTSTAGE is data (an exit's funcStageChange, a
     boss's end script, the gate disc; the port's own departures post
     PLAYERPOINT SETGENERATEPOS and STAGECTL NEXTSTAGE with delay 10,
     `online_exits.cpp` 147-148): no single place, and the relay has not
     decided yet. Not here.
  2. *The engine's stage request.* STAGECTL NEXTSTAGE
     (`StageCtlManager::command`, `managers_core.cpp` 1102-1129: the picture
     black, SESTOP / ENVSTOP, the randomizer's zone remap 1115-1125, then
     `Engine::request_stage`, `engine.cpp` 660-666) sets `pending_stage_`;
     SETGENERATEPOS set `PlayerPointManager::point_no_` before it
     (`managers_core.cpp` 3130-3133; first.lua reads it through
     PLAYERgetPos, 3707-3716, and the player's GENERATE through GETMATRIX).
     After that step the client parks (`Session::park`, `session.cpp`
     1237-1275, the BARRIER with the target and point it read) and steps
     the engine no more until BARRIER_OK. Still before the relay's answer.
  3. *BARRIER_OK, before the next step* (`Session::on_barrier_ok` ->
     `set_barrier`, `session.cpp` 1277): the first place that knows the
     decision. Then the transition steps: the module reload
     (`engine.cpp` 1994-2023, its length from the departing stage's files,
     not the target) with its held fields, then the load step: `apply_barrier`
     (the story's 503 rule reads `pending_stage_`, `online.cpp` 621) and
     `begin_stage_load`, which consumes `pending_stage_` (737) and takes the
     snapshot with `point_no` (819). The generate point: everything before
     `begin_stage_load`.

  `dw4_world_probe DATA redirect` (headless, online rules, stag0101 direct
  start, the departure posted at frame 1201, DISSOLVE answered at the park
  with the engine's own slot; the redirect is `request_stage` plus
  `PlayerPointManager::set_point_no`, which is all `redirect_pending_stage`
  has to do). Each stage group's redirects are compared with that group's
  own NEXTSTAGE stagML11 point 3: solo; a parked guest of a stage group of
  two and of three (present 3 and 7, own slot 1, as at a group DISSOLVE that
  leads home or an instance's end: present above one and an own slot other
  than 0 at BARRIER_OK, the slot moved to 0 only in `apply_barrier`); the
  zone shuffle. "Before the load step" is the last held field, after which
  the load step's first work is `apply_barrier` (`engine.cpp` 2062-2066):
  the top of `apply_barrier`. Logs `build/meas2/redirect_r1.log` (worktree
  `i1ameas`; the first run `build/meas/redirect1.log`):

  | Stage group | Departure | Redirect to stagml11 point 3 | Load snapshot (canonical) | Net fingerprints after the load |
  | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
  | solo, two, three | NEXTSTAGE stagML11 point 3 (each group's reference) | - | - | - |
  | solo | NEXTSTAGE stagML02 point 0 | at the park (place 3), after the first transition step, before the load step | equal (16,667 bytes) | equal, 3,978 frames |
  | two present, own slot 1 | NEXTSTAGE stagML02 point 0 | the same three places | equal (16,668 bytes) | equal, 3,977 frames |
  | three present, own slot 1 | NEXTSTAGE stag0102 point 0 | the same three places | equal (16,668 bytes) | equal, 3,977 frames |
  | solo, two, three | as above | the stage alone at the park, the point left at 0 | differs from byte 7,185 (the point) | differ from frame 1629 / 1650 / 1711 |
  | solo, zone shuffle on | NEXTSTAGE dng101b1 point 0 (remapped to dng102b1 by NEXTSTAGE) | at the park | equal to the zone-shuffle reference | equal |

  The park is the NEXTSTAGE's step (1202), the load step 21 steps later
  solo (1223: the module reload's 20 held fields) and 22 with two or three
  present (1224); after the load step the engine is solo (present 1) in
  every case: a redirect anywhere from BARRIER_OK to the top of
  `apply_barrier` gives the state of a NEXTSTAGE to that stage and point,
  bit for bit, for a parked guest of a group as for a solo engine, and it
  needs the generate point (a redirect of the stage alone puts the player
  at the old point number). The zone remap happens in NEXTSTAGE, so a
  redirect's target is taken as it is (right for a way home). **Design:**
  `redirect_pending_stage` is called from `on_barrier_ok` (before
  `set_barrier`'s first step) or at the very top of `apply_barrier`, never
  later (the 503 rule and the snapshot read the target there); it asserts
  that the barrier's decision is DISSOLVE and a stage change is pending,
  not a solo engine (at `on_barrier_ok` a parked guest's engine still has
  every present slot). The
  BARRIER already went out with the original target (the relay redirects,
  so it knows both); a HEADING sent for the original target is the relay's
  to drop.
- This closes 8.8's "barriers only add" for leaving: no engine takes the
  host's story, quest state or gate disc return home (invariant 5).

#### 19.8.4 Pending sets and the owner key

- The client's confirmed story follows the story owner of its current visit
  (BARRIER_OK names it): the own at home, the host's in an instance (the
  host keeper's STORY_ACK goes to every member of the instance).
- STORY carries the owner key (member id, box). The server refuses a STORY
  whose key is not the sender's current owner (reason *owner*, not sent
  again).
- Progress made at home goes up with the own key before the BARRIER that
  leaves the hub stage (as every barrier sends STORY first, 6.3).
- A value that waits only for the visit age or a spacing is queued for its
  owner (round 59's earned values, round G's *queued*), so it is not lost
  when the next engine story is a host's.

#### 19.8.5 Guests' progress and the host away

- Guests' progress counts for the host (8.3-8.8 with the guest rules): the
  rooms' "any player counts", now for the instance's host.
- The host is in his instance or in his grace, always. The grace holds
  guests' values (8.6's *hold*): merged when the host returns, discarded at
  the end; the guests' engines go home and are replaced, so nothing lingers.
  From the END on (any reason: `host_left`, `host_lost`, `staff`, a story
  replaced) a guest's STORY is refused (reason *owner*), also while its
  seat waits for its DISSOLVE (fix-019; before, it still merged into the
  host's keeper once the hold was released). The host's own values stay
  his (his keeper is his own story), also when his stage group did not
  answer the END's HOME and was detached (fix-019's refix: fix-019 first
  refused them there as another's story).
  Therefore round 59's *not_started*, start epochs, `OwnerSeen` and
  `OwnerEnters`, the dropped sets with their drop epochs, BARRIER_OK's
  dropped set and `Rooms:StoryWhileOwnerAway` retire: a new account's home
  simply starts at zero (its own story is empty; 8.6's "an owner without a
  story starts at zero" holds by construction).
- The phase steps 1-6 happen only in stagML02 and stagML11 (8.7), which are
  always home: a phase step is always the player's own. A guest adds field
  progress to the host's story (bosses, world events, key items, the
  training's 503) and at most flag 86 from stagBS06 under round 59's clear
  rule.

#### 19.8.6 Same story point (Q6)

- **The story point** = (difficulty, phase, the main-line flags M, K0-K10).
  M is a new census class `mainline` in `data/online/story_sets.json`: the
  bosses 67-70 and the world events 19-20, 22, 35, 49, 82-83, 320-327,
  329-335, 383, 404-408. Not in M: the Numemon 89-99, the intros 501-507,
  503, the quest clears 426-452, the quest boards 469-474, the quest line's
  rewards, COUNTER 1 and 7. A freed Numemon or a watched intro must not
  separate two players who stand before the same boss (question 33).
- **The mirror.** When the host's keeper accepts a delta made in a visit,
  every guest present in that visit for at least `World:MirrorMinSeconds`
  (30) whose own story point equals the host's *before* the merge gets
  into its own keeper the part of the accepted delta that **its own STORY
  for the same visit also reported** (the phase, every flag of it, side
  content included, the keys; no counters): not spaced (two lockstep
  engines of one visit made the same delta), history reason *mirror*,
  notice "Shared story progress saved to your story." once per stage.
  Equal points stay equal, so a pair before the same boss keeps getting the
  progress together. Spectators never; a guest at any other point nothing.
  Values held in the host's grace mirror when they merge.
- **Joiners count from their JOIN** (round 72's review). A member that
  entered the visit by a JOIN (a walk-in, a travel, *Go along*) holds
  through its restore everything the visit set before, and 8.3's pending
  set carries those values as its own ("progress a member's engine adopted
  through a join is pending"). So the client keeps the persistent shared
  values of its restored state as the visit's *join base*, and STORY marks
  which of its values are in it (I2). The mirror intersects the accepted
  delta only with the values the guest's engine set after its JOIN tick: a
  member who goes along after Kim's boss fell, stays 30 s and is in step
  gets nothing of that boss. Base-group members and co-arrivals load the
  visit's snapshot, which holds only confirmed values, so their base adds
  nothing. The host's keeper still merges adopted values by the guest rules
  (sets, harmless twice); they only never reach a mirror. W16c checks it.
- **Why the guest's own report.** The host's STORY is the owner's and not
  spaced (round 59's exemption). Mirrored on its own, a modified host
  client could write into the own stories of every in-step guest, where
  before it could only spoil its own. With the intersection a value reaches
  a guest's own story only when the guest's own engine made it in the same
  shared simulation; a value only the host claims stays the host's.
- **The order** at a barrier into a hub stage is fixed in 19.8.3: STORY of
  every member, the host's merge, the mirror, then the in-step test and the
  replace payloads.
- **Computed on the server** from stored stories; the client claims
  nothing. The C# rule, a Python twin and golden vectors in
  `data/online/story_point_golden.json`. The prompt's and the browser's
  *Same story point* badge comes from the same test (the viewer's own point
  against the host's); in the prompt's order it is only the last
  tie-breaker (19.7.3).
- Round I2 builds it; until then a guest's own story gets nothing from an
  instance.

#### 19.8.7 The host's settings

- **What.** The host's box's difficulty (chosen at his Game Start in the
  original dialog, limited by the box's own clears; the server rebases his
  story onto it, 8.7), the randomizer seed and modes (1.1: a host setting),
  camera mode, light mode and fast loading (Online > Settings; they apply at
  home and in every instance he hosts).
- **How they travel.** BARRIER_OK of a JOIN or a co-arrival and STATE_DATA
  carry them; the joiner's engine takes them with the state; DISSOLVE sets
  its own back (19.8.3). The handshake's settings hash goes (sent as 0); each
  stage group has its settings hash, part of its snapshot's canonical form,
  and every engine construction and restore sets `cheats_` and the modes
  from it (6.12).
- **Round I1a's first task.** Which of them the engine reads only at a stage
  load or at construction (camera data aaaCamera / aaaCameraL, the light,
  the loader's timing, the randomizer's NEXTSTAGE remap and enemy tables),
  and whether a restore with them equals a Game Start with them (hidden
  two-client runs per setting, fingerprints). A setting that fails becomes a
  join filter (rows *Other settings*, greyed) until a later round fixes it.
- **Measured r71.** Where each setting is read (code, and the stage
  descriptors in the game data: 98 of them pick `aaaCamera.igb` /
  `aaaCameraL.igb` by SYSgetCameraMode, `generatorN/H/V.igb` by
  SYSgetDifficulty and a light pack by SYSgetLightMode; start.lua's
  funcStartLayerSet sets LIGHTCTRL SETCOLOR by the light mode):

  | Setting | Where | Read when |
  | --- | --- | --- |
  | difficulty | `GameSystem::difficulty` (SYSgetDifficulty, `managers_core.cpp` 3706) | the stage load (the descriptor's generator file; stag0101: generatorn / generatorv) and scripts (flags 406+) |
  | camera mode | `GameSystem::camera_mode` (SYSgetCameraMode, 3720) | the stage load (the descriptor's camera file) |
  | light mode | `GameSystem::light_mode` (SYSgetLightMode, 3820) | the stage load (stag0101 / stagML11: `ls_pack` for 0, `lh_pack` for 1) and start.lua |
  | fast loading | `Cheats::fast_loading` | latched at `begin_stage_load` (`loader_fast_`, `engine.cpp` 800) and read at NEXTSTAGE for the module reload's length (1997) |
  | randomizer enemies | `Cheats::rand_seed` / `rand_enemies` | the load (the donor packages, `engine.cpp` 1822), every enemy GENERATE (298) and wave (`generater.cpp` 237-330) |
  | randomizer zones | `rand_zones` | NEXTSTAGE (`managers_core.cpp` 1115-1125) |
  | randomizer drops | `drop_seed` | every drop (`generater.cpp` 339-377) |

  A restore (`GameEngineLink::restore`, `engine_adapter.cpp` 269-285) takes
  the modes with the snapshot's GameSystem (`Engine::restore`, `engine.cpp`
  864-869) and the cheats with the snapshot (850; `begin_stage_load` latches
  the snapshot's fast loading for the load in progress), and then
  `start_online` applies the joiner's **own** settings over the cheats
  (`apply_room_cheats(settings_, ...)`, 301: the rooms' assumption that
  every member has the same). A checkpoint join's tick state brings the
  host's cheats back at T (`tick_state.cpp` 468), after the load ticks ran
  with the joiner's own.

  `dw4_world_probe DATA settings` (headless, online rules): a host's Game
  Start with settings H (the modes as `after_live_step` writes them, the
  cheats as `start_online` sets them) direct into stag0101, the field's
  dungeon entrance (SETGENERATEPOS 0, NEXTSTAGE dng101b1) at the load step
  + 1100; a joiner restores the stag0101 load snapshot through
  `GameEngineLink::restore` with its own settings J and replays the pads
  (4,199 frames compared, the stage change at 1102); a second joiner takes
  round J's path (the load ticks to K, the host's tick state at T = 901).
  Log `build/meas/settings3.log`.

  | Host H / joiner J | Classic join (restore + log) | Checkpoint join |
  | --- | --- | --- |
  | the same (defaults; and all non-default on both: Very Hard, camera 1, light 0, fast loading, randomizer 4242 with all three) | equal | equal |
  | J fast loading, H not (and the reverse) | differ from the stage change + 1 (the module reload's length) | equal (T brings H's cheats) |
  | J randomizer, H not (and the reverse; another seed) | differ from the next load (+21; the zones: another stage, dng102b1 against dng101b1; another seed: +59) | refused: `apply_tick_state` "a document id beyond the engine's files" (the donor packages) or "structure", then the classic path |
  | H enemies only / zones only | differ from the next load / take another stage | refused (enemies) |
  | H drops only | equal for 4,199 frames (no drop happened; by code the first drop differs) | - |
  | H Very Hard, J Normal | equal (the snapshot's GameSystem) | equal |
  | the same, J's own modes applied after the restore | differ from load + 351 (the first wave: generatorn instead of generatorv) | - |
  | H camera 1 / light 0, J's own modes applied | equal for 4,199 frames (stag0101 has no camera file; in dng101b1 the joiner loaded the other camera file and stayed equal for the 3,000 frames there; the light packs did not change the load's timing here) | - |

  And the way back (corrected after the review; `build/meas2/settings_r1.log`,
  the first run `build/meas/settings3.log`): a stag0101 visit on settings
  H, its DISSOLVE to stagML11 point 3 parked, the own settings O set at the
  park (the modes and `apply_room_cheats`), against the same departure
  with O all along, both ways and with fast loading:

  | H / O | Module reload (park to load step) | Fast loading the load latched | Files of the stagML11 load | Settings held after the load |
  | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
  | H all non-default (Very Hard, camera 1, light 0, fast loading, randomizer 4242 with all three) / O default | 59 steps; O all along 21; H kept 1 | off, as O | O's 9 files (`lh_pack`; H kept loads `ls_pack`) | O's |
  | H default / O all non-default | 1 step, as O all along (H kept 21) | on, as O | O's 9 files | O's |
  | H all non-default but fast loading / O default | 59 steps; O all along 21; H kept 59 | off, as O | O's 9 files | O's |

  So the own settings set at the park give the files, the fast-loading
  latch and the settings of a Game Start with them, and the module
  reload's fast-loading choice is O's too. The reload's length is not a
  setting's: it follows the departing visit's files (`loader_teardown_cost`,
  `engine.cpp` 1997), 59 steps after the visit on H (other files: the
  difficulty's generator, the camera and light files, the randomizer's
  donor packages; which of them adds the steps was not split), 21 after
  one on the defaults; and the stagML11 load then took 448
  frames against 408 with O all along. A DISSOLVE load is the member's own
  solo load (nobody replays it), so this history is fine; a Game Start's
  timing it is not. (Fingerprints of these runs are not compared: their
  stag0101 visits ran on different settings, so their states differ.)

  **What it means for a joiner, and the design changes (r71):** every
  setting is the stage group's, i.e. the host's, while a member plays in
  the instance: the modes need nothing (the snapshot and the tick state
  carry the host's GameSystem); the cheats (randomizer, fast loading) are
  in the snapshot and the tick state too, so **no BARRIER_OK or STATE_DATA
  field is needed for them**: a restore must keep the snapshot's cheats
  (only the forced-off cheats of `online_cheats`), and `start_online` after
  a restore must stop applying the member's own `RoomSettings`; that one
  line is what breaks a join with other settings today. The same holds for
  the session's other restores in an instance (a fallback to the member's
  own solo load, `session.cpp` 1344-1355 and 1448-1450: that load ran on
  the host's settings too) and for a guest whose stage group a co-arrival
  takes as its base (its engine holds the host's). No setting needs a join
  filter. The member's own settings come back only at the DISSOLVE,
  set in the parked stage change before the module reload (19.8.3's park):
  the load then reads the files and latches the fast loading of a Game
  Start with them (the reload's length and the load's duration follow the
  departing visit, above). The light mode measured as
  presentation only; it stays a host setting until a round checks that no
  stage's light packs change the original loading's timing.
- Lists show "Hard", "Very Hard", "Randomizer".

#### 19.8.8 Quests (question 35)

- The prompt matches only equal session contexts (3.7): a quest player sees
  instances on the same quest, a story player story instances. A quest
  board's start lists only instances on that quest.
- A travel (browser, friend list, party) may cross contexts in *help mode*:
  at the join the joiner's own context values (3.7's class: 409, 376-381,
  384-389, 424, 571, COUNTER 2, folder 11 and the rest) go into its carry
  with the personal ones, and at DISSOLVE they come back. It helps and keeps
  its EXP, items and Bits; the quest's end and reward run only in lobbies
  that took the quest. Rows: *Quest: <name>*.

#### 19.8.9 Rewards, quest boards, achievements, uploads

- **Rewards.** The quest line's first rewards and the keychain are set only
  in the hub stages ML11-13 (8.8), which now always run the own story, and
  stories are per box (answer 11 (b)), so they are per box by construction
  (answer 9). Round G's `online_rewards` store and 9.1.9's store are not
  built; `form_reward` reads the box's story. A field delta never holds a
  reward flag, so the mirror never copies one.
- **Quest boards** use the own tiers, in a party too. Answer 10 (b) ("the
  higher of the guest's and the host's values") had a guest standing at the
  room's board; in the world every board is in a hub stage, which is always
  home, so nobody stands at a foreign board and the rule has no case. A
  party member reaches the leader's higher quests by helping in them (a
  co-arrival with the leader or a travel, help mode, 19.8.8). The leader's
  tiers are never written into a member's lobby engine: that would put
  foreign story into an own engine (invariant 3), and a hub STORY with the
  own key would make it permanent.
- **Achievements.** A borrowed story gives none (8.8); "was there" event
  achievements come from live steps; story challenges count only for the
  host; `PlayContext.RoomCode` / `RoomPlayers` become `InstanceId` /
  `InstancePlayers` / `IsHost` (11); `online_join` is "joined someone else's
  instance", `online_host` "hosted with at least three players"; the
  randomizer ruleset comes from the instance's settings; old unlocks keep
  `room_id`, new ones fill `instance_id` (the server maps the relay's `wid`
  to the history id, 19.17.2; the client's `wid` is never stored).
- **Achievements need a new session check, or nothing unlocks after I1.**
  `Play:RequireRoom` is true in `appsettings.json` and in the production
  example, and `AchievementService.CheckSessionAsync` proves online play
  through `rooms` / `room_members` (`FindMembershipAsync`), the room's
  ranked data hash and its randomizer ruleset; `RoomStoryHoldsClearAsync`
  asks `relay.Story(roomCode)`. Without rooms every unlock, and
  `EvaluateStateAsync` at an upload, would fail with `room_required`. Round
  I1's server lane replaces it: `Play:RequireWorld` (true; `RequireRoom` is
  read as it for one release), and the context comes from the relay through
  `WorldService.PlayContext(account)`: in the world within the last minute,
  the `wid` and its history id, the players of the last minute, `IsHost`,
  the instance's settings and whether its data hash is ranked. The clear
  check runs against the requester's own keeper (a guest's clear counts
  when it was mirrored into his own story, 19.8.6). Integration tests:
  *Lone Tamer* alone, `online_host` with three guests, a story clear as
  the host and as an in-step guest, and none for a not-in-step guest.
- **An engine on another's story without a seat there** (fix-019's
  refix: a removed member until its HOME, a fallback from nobody's
  instance until its way home, a JOIN whose seat went) is that instance's
  guest in the play context: its `wid` and history id, `IsHost` false, its
  settings (randomizer, difficulty), the players of its stage group. Before,
  it read as at home on its own story (`wid` 0, `IsHost` true, its own
  settings), so story challenges and the ruleset counted as the own while
  the engine held the former host's story and settings. The 0.1.8 client's
  own facts still say "home" there (its BARRIER_OK names no instance); the
  API decides by the relay's context.
- **Uploads** are unchanged: the server composes the own story into every
  record and ignores uploaded story bytes (8.4); round G's card store
  override and the own story bytes in `CharacterSync` stay as a net (hubs
  hold the own story anyway, so the save room writes it).
