### 19.9 Travel: joins next to the host (round I3)

#### 19.9.1 GOTO

The browser, the friend list's *Join*, a party's *Follow*, the Online menu's
*Go to Kim* and a seat rejoin send GOTO (request id, mode, target: an
instance or a member). The relay checks Visible() (19.7.2), that the
instance is not ending and that a seat is free (or held or reserved for the
requester); a boss-locked target is a wait. GOTO_RESULT answers *ok* with a
one-time token and the target's stage, or the reason. A hidden, blocked or
private target is always "not found". A GOTO to a member of the
requester's own instance (mode 4 *go to host*, mode 8 *go to member*,
round 72) is no departure toward home: it is answered *ok* without a token
and stamped as GO (19.9.6).

#### 19.9.2 The departure

- Leaving an instance asks first: "Leave Kim's instance and join Lee?"; a
  host reads "This ends your instance for your guests."
- The departure goes toward home: at home (a solo hub instance, never
  joined or logged) the client starts it itself,
  `Engine::online_depart_home()`: the gate disc's records without
  SYSsetGateStage (SQ_EXIT, fade, NEXTSTAGE stagML11 point 3), from the
  lobby to its own gate as well; in an instance (a travel into another
  instance) it is the member's *Leave instance* (INTENT 3, the relay stamps
  HOME for its slot, 19.6.5); a travel inside the own instance never
  leaves it (19.9.6). Its BARRIER carries the token. The engine parks at the barrier tick, before
  its transition steps (6.7).
- The relay holds the barrier until the target stage group is joinable and
  its target slot has a safe position (19.9.3), at most
  `Instances:JoinHoldSeconds` (30). A boss lock waits without that limit:
  "Kim is in a boss fight. Waiting...", *B: Back to the lobby*, *X: Join Lee
  instead* when another member is in a stage group without the lock.
- **JOIN:** the client first keeps a snapshot of its parked engine (as the
  spectator keeps its lobby, 19.14: a solo hub or a solo field engine at a
  barrier, never logged), then restores the target without running the
  lobby's transition (round J: from a checkpoint, under a second; before J:
  snapshot and log as today, refused beyond `MaxCatchUpSeconds` with "too
  long to join"). Today a joiner runs its own transition first and keeps
  that load as its fallback (3.4); for a travel the kept snapshot is the
  fallback.
- **Failure before the restore** (ended, full, no longer open, the hold ran
  out): DISSOLVE; the parked engine runs its own transition into its lobby:
  "Couldn't join Kim: <reason>." **Failure after the restore** (the join's
  `LostGap` or `FallbackNew` paths, a checkpoint that fails twice): the
  client restores the kept snapshot, still parked at its barrier, and runs
  its transition into its lobby the same way. Never NEW: a NEW there could
  put the player alone into a stage his own story never reached
  (invariant 6).

#### 19.9.3 Spawning next to a slot

- The JOIN event gets a spawn kind: the entrance point (today, 0xFF) or
  *next to slot k* (0-3).
- Every present slot has a *safe position* in the online block of the
  snapshot and of the tick state, updated every step, online only: its
  position at its last step on the ground, outside a pit mat, not in a
  demo, a warp or a scene.
- At the JOIN tick every engine takes the first free offset of a fixed ring
  around slot k's safe position (behind, left, right, in front, at 1.2
  units), each checked with the stage's ground query in that order; none
  free: the safe position itself. The joiner faces the way slot k faces;
  PLAYER GENERATE and PLAYER2 GENESTAGE with that matrix, then SQ_ENTR, the
  rest as 6.6. Computed from the shared state, the same on every machine.
- A defeated target, or one at a barrier: the living member with the most
  others around it. No safe position yet (it just arrived): the entrance
  nearest to it. A target in a pit or in mid-jump does not hold the join:
  the joiner appears at its last safe position. No invulnerability is added
  (the original has none at an entrance); scenario W14 records a join next
  to fighting enemies.
- **Nobody alive.** While every present slot of the target stage group is
  defeated (STATE's flag *no living member*, 19.18, which round I1b's go
  along brings), the relay holds the JOIN (the travel's hold, 19.9.2) until one
  lives again or the group's game over takes it home (then the travel
  follows the instance as in 19.9.4's "the target took a barrier", or ends
  in the lobby when the instance ended). No rescue joins: a join never
  turns a game over the original would run into a fight that goes on.
- The camera is the joiner's own box camera at the spawn (4.1).
- Walk-ins keep the entrance point (19.7.7); only travels spawn next to a
  member.

#### 19.9.4 Races

| Case | Answer |
| --- | --- |
| Boss lock | wait until the fight ends, *Join <member> instead*, or *B* (home) |
| Full meanwhile | "Kim's instance is full." (home); staff: *Spectate* |
| The target took a barrier while the joiner loaded | the join follows it to its new stage (one more hold); a second move: home |
| Visibility changed, blocked or removed meanwhile | "The instance is not open to you anymore." (home) |
| The instance ended | "The instance has ended." (home) |
| The host in his grace | hold until he is back, or home at the end |
| Every member of the target stage group defeated | hold until one lives, or follow the group's game over (19.9.3) |

#### 19.9.5 Timing

Before round J a travel catches up as a join does today (1.3 s after one
minute of the visit, 31 s after thirty). With J it takes under a second at
any visit length. The user's P3 puts J before round I3.

#### 19.9.6 Travel inside the own instance (round 72)

A member who travels to another member of its own instance (*Go along*,
round I1b, 19.30.7; *Go to <member>*, round I3) never leaves the instance:
no *Leave instance*, no HOME, its seat stays taken, its engine keeps the
host's story. The relay holds the request until the target's stage group
is joinable and has a living member and the member's own stage group can
take the event (19.30.7, step 2; the member plays on meanwhile), then
stamps GO (slot, stage, point) in the member's stage group with the
target's stage and the point through which the target's stage group
entered it; the engine runs the exit port's departure for the GO slots of
that step, with an exit's side rule (`ForkKind::go`, 19.30.7). Its barrier
is one inside the instance: the target's stage group first (a co-arrival
or a JOIN; from round I3 with the spawn next to the target's slot, 19.9.3),
waited for while it exists, without `Instances:JoinHoldSeconds`; only when
nobody of the instance is at that stage any more, a new stage group of the
instance there. Never home, never a new instance, never a second stage
group of the instance next to a living one on the same stage: invariant
6's round 72 sentence allows it, the target being where the instance's
story is.

- GOTO mode 4 *go to host* and mode 8 *go to member* inside the own
  instance answer GOTO_RESULT *ok* without a token and stamp GO; a target
  in a hub stage (a defeated host in his return hold, 19.6.5) or at a
  barrier is "not found" or a short wait for its arrival.
- 19.9.4's races apply, except that a failure lands in a new stage group
  of the instance at the target's stage (when nobody of the instance is
  there any more), not home; a target that took a barrier while the joiner
  loaded is followed once (from round I3), as there.
- **Before round I3 the minimum is *Go along*** (19.30.7): the GO event,
  the JOIN at the entrance and round J's checkpoint join (merged). Nothing
  of I3's travel (GOTO, the kept snapshot, the spawn next to a slot) is
  needed for it.

### 19.10 The instance browser NPC (round I3)

- **Where.** stagML11 beside the area gate (`mate00`), on walkable ground
  outside every mat and hit trigger, visible from the gate; I3 measures the
  spot from the stage's collision and points. `data/online/browser_npc.json`
  holds the package, stage, position, facing and tag.
- **The figure.** A Digi-Elf from the lobby's own `n_digilff` package with
  the tag "Instances", made and drawn by the ghost figure renderer (12.1):
  presentation only, never in the simulation, no collision. One figure from
  the game's data and no other new content. First task: the renderer takes
  an NPC package (today it takes player form packages). Fallback without a
  figure: the Online menu's *Instances* page alone.
- **Opening it.** Within about 1.5 units and facing it, "A: Instances"
  shows; A opens the window. The press is held from the pad stream: the
  lobby is a solo hub instance, never joined or logged, and the reach
  excludes every NPC talk trigger.
- **The window** (ImGui in the menu's colours, controller first): tabs
  *All*, *Party and friends* and one per area (LB/RB; an instance is under
  its own area, 19.30.2: a Death Valley instance whose host is in the
  Fortress or on the Power Plant plateau stays under Death Valley); **one
  row per instance** (not per stage group): host, area and the host's
  stage, players x/4 across all its stage groups, story point, ping, state
  and age, the
  states of 19.7.2; sorted as 19.7.3 without its arrival-stage keys (the
  browser has no arrival stage); *A* opens a row's details (the
  members with their stages) with *Join* focused (two presses, so a stray A
  never leaves the lobby); *Y* refreshes, and the list refreshes every 2 s
  while open (BROWSE at most once a second). Staff see every instance, the
  private ones marked, and *Spectate* and *Join as moderator* (19.7.2).
- **Join** is a travel (19.9) and always goes to the host: the loading
  screen reads "Joining Kim...", and the player appears next to the host,
  in whichever stage the host is (P3: "teleports you directly to the
  leader"). A member in another stage group is reached through *Join
  <member>* in the details or the friend list. No story requirement (Q5):
  the row shows the story point and *Same story point*.
- **The same browser** is the title's *Instances* screen (where *Join*
  starts the session and travels after the Game Start) and the Online menu's
  *Instances* page anywhere at home. Inside an instance it lists, and *Join*
  asks to leave the instance first.
- Nothing pauses while it is open (round 63).

### 19.11 Friends and blocks (round I2)

**The model.**

- A request from A to B that B accepts makes a friendship (one row). A
  request from B while A's to B is open accepts both at once. Decline is
  silent for the sender: the declined row stays and looks "sent" to him
  until it expires with the pending ones (`Friends:RequestDays`, 30), then
  both are purged; a new request from him meanwhile answers "Request sent."
  and changes nothing. (A declined row purged after 24 h would tell the
  sender by its disappearance.) Either side removes; the other is not told
  and sees it in his list.
- **Incoming cap.** At most `Friends:MaxPendingIn` (100) open requests
  reach one account at a time. A request beyond it answers "Request sent."
  like any other and waits undelivered (`delivered = 0`) until a place frees
  (an accept, decline, cancel, block or expiry), oldest first; a blocked
  player's silent request neither counts nor moves up while the block lasts.
  The cap is never an answer to a sender. (Changed in round I2-social after
  its review: the earlier answer "<name> can't take more friend requests
  right now." let a sender probe a block or a decline through whether his
  own request takes a place, by cancelling and sending again into a full
  inbox or by a second account sending right after him; 19.25.)
- Requests name the exact account name (case-insensitive): no search, no
  partial match, so nobody can scrape the account list.

**Blocks.**

- A block removes the friendship and the blocker's own request, the pair
  from a common party, and the blocked player from an instance the blocker
  hosts (19.6.6). The blocked player's request to the blocker no longer
  reaches him but stays "sent" for its sender (`delivered = 0`; a vanishing
  row would reveal the block); an unblock delivers it when the blocker has a
  place (round I2-social, 19.25: the design said "removes the requests in
  both directions", which a vanishing row would have revealed).
- From then on, both ways: no instance in the prompt, the browser or the
  friend list, no join, no travel, no co-arrival, no ghost figure, no invite,
  no request, no whereabouts.
- A block is never revealed: a blocked sender's request answers "Request
  sent." and stays in his outgoing list (`delivered = 0`), never shown to
  the receiver; his invite answers "<name> is not available.", the same text
  as for an offline player.
- A block does not throw anyone out of an instance they share (except the
  blocker's own as host); *Leave instance* is always there.
- Staff respect blocks while they play; only an explicit moderation action
  (*Spectate*, *Join as moderator*, *End*, *Remove*) passes a block, and it
  is audited (19.7.2, 19.14). A griefer who blocks every moderator is still
  reachable, and nobody is followed by a blocked moderator without a logged
  reason.

**Limits** (per account): 200 friends; 50 open outgoing requests; 100 open
incoming requests; requests 20 per hour and 100 per day; requests (pending
and declined) expire after 30 days; 500 blocks; other social calls 60 per
minute; `GET /friends` once per 2 s.

**Whereabouts.**

- FRIENDS_STATE (relay, on change, at most once per 2 s per friend): each
  online friend's name, area and stage ("Kim is in Cliff Dungeon B3"), "In
  the lobby", "Title screen", whether he is in an instance (host or guest,
  players x/4) and whether that instance is open to *this* viewer (the
  *Join* button).
- A Private instance shows "Playing" (no place) unless the viewer is in the
  host's party. A friend whose `whereabouts` preference is *nobody* shows
  only "Online". A staff member who spectates shows his lobby ("In the
  lobby"), never the watched instance (19.14).
- Offline friends ("last seen 2 days") and requests come over REST.

**Toasts** (at most one every 2 s, queued, none during an own scene):
"<name> wants to be your friend. View: Friends", "<name> accepted your
friend request.", "<name> is online." (switchable), "<name> joined your
instance.". Requests are summarized: at most one request toast a minute;
more than one new request since the last reads "<n> new friend requests.
View: Friends", and the queue never holds more than one request toast (so
a hundred requests are one toast, not two hundred seconds of them).

**Where.**

- The title's home screen: *Friends* (the list with *Join*, *Invite to
  party*, *Remove*, *Block*; tabs *Requests* with Accept / Decline and
  Cancel, *Add friend* by name with the on-screen keyboard, *Blocked* with
  Unblock).
- In the game: the Online menu's *Friends* page and the F1 Online tab, the
  same; the player card at a ghost figure or a present member.
- *Join* in the list is a travel (19.9), from the title after the Game
  Start; round I3 adds it (I2 shows the whereabouts).
- The website: 19.20.

### 19.12 Parties (round I4)

- **Size and invites.** Up to four, with a leader. Invite from the player
  card, the friend list, the *Nearby* page, the browser's member lists or by
  name. An invite lasts 60 s (no answer = declined), one at a time is shown,
  others queue. Not from or to blocked players; an invited player with
  `invites = friends` only takes friends' invites (others answer "Invite
  sent." and go nowhere). 10 invites per minute per sender, one open invite
  per pair, 3 per pair in 10 minutes.
- **Lifetime.** Relay memory only. It ends when one member is left or after
  `World:PartyIdleMinutes` (10) with every member offline; a server restart
  ends every party.
- **Leader.** The leader can *Promote* and *Remove*; a leader who leaves or
  is gone 60 s hands the party to the member who has been in it longest.
  Parties hand over, instances do not.
- **The party's instance.** Through the gate together the party lands in a
  new instance its leader hosts (P4). When the leader himself chooses a
  foreign instance (a prompt row, the browser, a friend's *Join*), that is
  the party's instance as long as he is in it, and the members follow him
  there as guests where seats allow: an extension of P4 for the case P4
  does not name, which keeps the party together instead of splitting it.
- **Travel.**
  - Members who take the gate within the co-arrival window of the leader
    co-arrive with him, whatever the visibility; the leader is the host and
    his group is always the base (19.6.1), even when a member reaches the
    barrier first: a member's barrier toward the stage the leader's HEADING
    names waits for the leader's barrier (at most
    `Instances:CoArrivalHoldMs` after that HEADING, or
    `World:StartingSeconds` while the leader's new instance starts), and
    the member is spawned in the leader's load step. Without the leader's
    HEADING the member is an ordinary fresh arrival (the party's instance,
    if any, is its prompt's top row).
  - Members at home elsewhere get the notice "Kim is heading to Cliff
    Dungeon B1. Follow?  View: answer" (20 s on screen like the go-along
    notice, `World:AnswerNoticeSeconds`; no answer = stay;
    the *Party* page answers it, A: *Follow*, B: *Stay*): the go-along
    notice's form (19.30.6), because A and B are the game's buttons
    (19.5.7). *Follow* is a travel: a co-arrival while the leader's base
    still holds, else a join next to the leader.
  - A member who arrives from home in the area of the party's instance
    enters it without a prompt (at its stage group at the arrival stage,
    else as a guest there where 19.30.3's visited rule allows); the party's
    instance in another area is the prompt's top row.
  - Inside the instance party members are members like any: they get the
    go-along offers and are never pulled along (19.30.8).
  - The party's instance is always visible to its members (Private = party
    only).
- **Reserved seats.** An instance whose host is in a party keeps a seat for
  each online party member not in it ("+1 reserved"); strangers take what is
  left.
- **The leader's prompt** applies to the whole arriving party: *Join* only
  where all of it fits.
- **Quest boards:** each member's own tiers; the leader's higher quests by
  helping in them (19.8.9).
- **UI.** The Online menu's *Party* page (members with whereabouts and HP,
  *Join* per member, *Leave party*, the leader's *Promote*, *Remove* and,
  proposal 4 of 19.26, *Gather*), a small strip in the lobby, PARTY_STATE.
- **Discord** (13): the party size, else the instance's x/4; the state
  "In the lobby" or "<area>: <stage>".

### 19.13 The lobby as a meeting place

- **Server.** Each hub stage's cell (19.17.4) keeps its occupants with their
  last PRESENCE2 positions. Once a second each receiver's selection is
  recomputed: party, then friends, then the nearest, at most
  `World:HubFigures` (30) (Q10); never a pair with a block, a spectator, a
  hidden or loading member (spectating staff keep their lobby engine, but
  are never selected). A figure stays selected until it is 20 % farther
  than the 30th candidate, so figures do not pop. The fan-out sends a
  sender's PRESENCE2 to the receivers that selected it (an index per sender)
  instead of today's loop over every member of a room.
- **Rates.** The nearest 10 of a receiver get every packet (10 Hz while
  moving), the others every second one (5 Hz); presence has its own budget
  per receiver (`World:PresenceBytesPerSecond`, 24 KiB), apart from the
  64 KB/s bucket of game frames. About 12 KB/s per receiver at 30 figures
  (estimate), 2.4 MB/s for 200 players in lobbies. Measured r71 (19.17.4,
  redone after the review): a PRESENCE2 the hub forwards is 82 bytes with
  its header, so these rates (200 frames a second) are about 16 KB/s per
  receiver, 3.3 MB/s for 200; every one of 30 figures at 10 Hz would be
  about 25 KB/s, just over the 24 KiB budget.
- **MEMBER_INFO** (name, level, relation flags) goes before a figure's first
  packet to a receiver.
- **Client.** `GhostFigures::kMaxFigures` 9 becomes 30 and `kMaxWeapons` 16
  becomes 32. There is no low LOD to fall back on: a player form's igLod
  holds the full model and the "Kage" shadow proxy only
  (`scene_graph.cpp`, `ghost_figures.cpp`). So figures beyond the nearest
  10 skin and advance their animation every second frame (half rate; their
  positions still interpolate every frame), and the nearest 10 run at full
  rate. Round I1 measures 30 figures at 144 Hz on the reference machine
  (hidden; budget 1.5 ms per frame) with and without the half rate, and
  caps the drawn count by distance (the farthest first, down to 20) if it
  is still over; the cap is a client setting the F1 menu shows.
- **Measured r71: 30 figures.** A Release build without DW4_ONLINE_DEV
  with the test-only build option `DW4_GHOST_PROBE` (`ghost_figures.hpp`,
  `game_main.cpp`; never in a player build): `DW4_PROBE_GHOSTS=30` stands 30
  figures of the 16 forms (three of four with a weapon, every second one
  running a 10-unit circle) on a spiral around the own player in stagML11
  (direct start, no online session), `DW4_PROBE_GHOSTS_FULL=10` poses the
  nearest 10 every draw and the others every second draw (the half rate).
  Hidden window, `DW4_DEV_PRESENT=144` (a virtual 144 Hz: 0.42 steps a
  pass), the pass time from the pass's start to after the swap with a
  `glFinish` first (the GPU's work counts), 720 passes a report, the
  reports after the forms loaded; Ryzen 7 7800X3D, GeForce RTX 5070 Ti
  (OpenGL 3.3, driver 621.01), other rounds running beside it. Logs
  `build/meas/g_r1_*.log`, `g_r2_*.log`.

  The ranges are over a run's nine reports after the first (ten a run; the
  forms load in the first; `build/meas/g_table.py`):

  | Figures | Pass mean / p99, 1920x1080 | Pass mean / p99, 2560x1440 MSAA 4 | Figures' CPU a pass (update + draw), 1080p | of it pose / traversal |
  | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
  | none (two runs) | 0.57-0.72 / 0.81-0.94 ms | 0.67-0.82 / 0.92-1.11 ms | - | - |
  | 9 (today's cap) | 0.71-0.78 / 0.97-1.12 ms | - | 0.08-0.10 ms | 0.03 / 0.04-0.05 ms |
  | 30, full rate | 0.97-1.08 / 1.34-1.55 ms | 1.07-1.14 / 1.54-1.65 ms | 0.25-0.30 ms | 0.09-0.11 / 0.13-0.16 ms |
  | 30, half rate beyond the nearest 10 | 0.97-1.05 / 1.40-1.55 ms | 1.10-1.20 / 1.56-1.69 ms | 0.22-0.25 ms | 0.06-0.07 / 0.13-0.15 ms |
  | 30 close together (2 units apart), full rate | 0.97-1.07 / 1.30-1.58 ms | 1.11-1.16 / 1.52-1.69 ms | 0.24-0.29 ms | 0.09-0.11 / 0.13-0.15 ms |
  | 30 close together, half rate | 1.00-1.09 / 1.40-1.64 ms | 1.11-1.19 / 1.55-1.77 ms | 0.22-0.26 ms | 0.06-0.08 / 0.13-0.16 ms |

  30 figures cost about 0.40-0.45 ms a pass in all (CPU and GPU), under a
  third of the 1.5 ms budget; they make 59 draw items (one skinned body
  each, and the weapons). The half rate as measured skipped only `pose()`
  of the 20 farther figures every second pass (`ghost_figures.cpp` 541-567:
  the animation's pose kept from the pass before); the traversal, which
  builds the skinning palette and draws the skinned bodies, ran for every
  figure every pass. It saved 0.03-0.04 ms, inside the noise of the pass
  time. Single passes of up to 9 ms in four of the 13 runs are the
  machine's other work (other rounds ran beside it). Limits of the
  measurement: one fast machine (the RTX 5070 Ti, a 7800X3D); a hidden
  window (the default framebuffer of a visible window, its presentation
  and its compositing were not measured); the iGPU of this PC and no
  weaker GPU measured. **Design change (r71, conditional after the
  review):** 30 figures at full rate by default; the half rate (which
  would have to skip the palette and the skinning too to save anything)
  and the distance cap with its F1 setting are not built in I1a, but stay
  designed as the fallback: a round that measures a weaker GPU (the iGPU,
  `DW4_GHOST_PROBE`, visible window) over the 1.5 ms budget builds the cap
  (`kMaxFigures` 30, `kMaxWeapons` 32 stay either way). The probe stays in
  the tree for that check.
- **Tags** coloured by relation (19.5.2); a lagging member's icon as today.
- **Known limit.** The lobby's layout depends on each player's own phase
  (`start.lua`), so a ghost from another phase can walk where the viewer's
  lobby has a closed door. Figures are look only; this is documented, not
  fixed.
- **Fields.** No presence of other instances (today's tags of room members
  in another instance of the same stage go). The members of the own
  instance in another stage group of the same stage keep their tags (12).
- The menu stages stagIS* show nobody, as today.

### 19.14 Staff (Q12)

- **The role.** `POST /world/enter` issues the relay ticket with the role
  *staff* when the account's role in the database is moderator or admin,
  *member* otherwise (`RelayTickets`, HMAC, one time, 60 s; today only
  `member`). Today `RelayTickets.Create` / `Redeem` take a room code that a
  channel pattern checks, and the handshake (`HandleAsync`) accepts only the
  role `member`: round I1's relay lane changes the channel to one fixed
  world channel and lets `HandleAsync` accept `staff` too (the role then
  rides on the member). The relay also listens to the account service
  in-process (`IWorldNotifier.AccountChanged`): a demotion, lock, ban or
  deletion counts at once (a ban or a deletion closes the connection and,
  for a host, ends his instance). The client never claims a role.
- **Seeing.** Staff see every instance in the prompt and the browser,
  Private and Friends ones labelled, and the website's admin list.
- **Playing** with a free seat: a normal guest regardless of visibility
  where he chooses the instance himself (a prompt row, I1b; the browser,
  I3); the automatic join and the co-arrivals treat a moderator who simply
  plays as a player (fix-019, 19.7.2). With a gold *Staff* tag (`World:StaffTagWhenPlaying`, true; members can
  tell a moderator is in their instance). Audit row `staff_join`. Blocks
  and removal bars count for a playing moderator as for anyone; *Join as
  moderator* passes them and is audited as `staff_join_override` with the
  block or bar it passed.
- **Spectating** (I3), when the instance is full or by choice: GOTO mode
  *spectate*, BARRIER_OK decision 5 SPECTATE. The client keeps a snapshot of
  its own lobby engine (a solo hub, never logged), takes the target stage
  group's checkpoint (round J) or snapshot and log as an observer, and
  follows SEALED or LIVE (the observer paths of 6.6) without ever sending
  JOIN: no slot, no INPUT, no PRESENCE, not in INSTANCE_INFO or any list
  players see, its NETFP never votes, no saves, uploads, achievements or
  story from that engine. It follows the watched member through forks and
  barriers, a GO's included (the relay sends the new stage group's
  state), and never gets a go-along offer (19.30.5). Camera: a member's
  box camera, LB/RB cycle; a free camera only as a picture: the simulation
  culls by the members' cameras (4.2), so actors that only the free camera
  sees stand still there (a limit, not a desync). *Stop watching* restores
  the kept lobby snapshot: the moderator stands where he was. At most
  `World:MaxSpectators` (2) per instance. Invisible to the players (Q12),
  everywhere: his friends see him "In the lobby" (FRIENDS_STATE gives a
  spectator's lobby, never the watched instance); the spectator role never
  appears in "Recently played with", the instance's member lists,
  `peak_players` or the website's instance pages for players (the history
  keeps the row with role `spectator` for the admin pages and the audit
  only); he is no ghost figure while he watches.
- **Audit** (`audit_log`, 19.17.1): `staff_join`, `staff_join_override`,
  `staff_spectate_start` / `staff_spectate_end` (with the instance, host,
  visibility, members and the duration), `staff_end_instance`,
  `staff_remove`.
- **Actions.** End an instance, remove a member: in the browser (staff
  rows) and on the website's admin pages.
- The privacy page says: "Moderators may join or watch any instance to
  moderate it; every look is logged."

### 19.15 Reconnect (P7)

- **Within `Relay:ReconnectSeconds` (10):** RESUME as today (6.10).
- **A guest beyond that** (round I1): LEAVE; its client continues alone
  from its engine as a new stage group of the same instance (6.10's
  "continues alone", inside the instance; its seat stays while it is
  connected). Today's `Connect` would make such a member a hub-mode
  placeholder with an empty stage: not logged, not joinable, in no cell,
  with wrong whereabouts. Round I1 files it instead as a solo-led stage
  group of its instance at the stage and visit its client names in the
  reconnect (the resume request carries them), in that stage's cell,
  joinable at its next barrier and with right whereabouts. Its old stage
  group plays on without it: until round I5 the two do not see each other
  until one of them takes a barrier where the other is (P7 is met for the
  instance, not yet for the stage; documented in the toast "Reconnected.
  You're playing apart from Kim until the next stage."). Round I5 (after J)
  rejoins it to its old stage group from a checkpoint (GOTO mode 5, next
  to its own last safe position). If the instance ended meanwhile: the
  home departure (19.6.10), "The instance has ended."
- **The host:** the 60 s grace (19.6.7).
- **After the world's member timeout** (`World:MemberTimeoutSeconds`, 35,
  as the room's; for a host in his grace only after the grace plus 10 s,
  19.6.7) the member leaves the world; round I5 keeps its *seat* for
  `World:SeatSeconds` (120): the instance shows "+1 reserved".
- **A crash** (round I5): the player logs in and presses *Play*. WELCOME
  names the held seat; the session runs the bound box's Game Start by itself
  and travels back (19.9): "Returning to Kim's instance...", B cancels
  within 3 s. *Choose character* with another box gives the seat up. The
  seat gone: home.
- **The host's crash within his grace** (I5): his client rejoins his own
  slot from a checkpoint (round J): LEAVE of the filled slot and JOIN next
  to its last safe position in one stamped tick; he stays host.

### 19.16 Privacy and abuse

| Threat | Rule |
| --- | --- |
| A stranger pushes a public host's story | the host's choice of visibility; *Remove* with the 10-minute bar; question 32's guard (boss and story starts only with the host) if the user wants it |
| A guest griefs (steals drops, blocks the way, spams joins) | *Remove*, blocks, Private, *Report*; drops stay first come as in the original; joins and travels limited to 6 per minute per account and 3 per instance and account in 10 minutes |
| A host griefs guests (ends at once) | guests keep their EXP, items and Bits (saved at the stage change); "Recently played with" lets them block or avoid him |
| A forged CHOICE or GOTO to an instance the client may not see | Visible(), the bars and the seats are checked at the decision |
| Friend request spam | the limits of 19.11, the decline cooldown, blocks, exact names only |
| Stalking through whereabouts | friends only, the `whereabouts` preference, Private shows "Playing", blocked players see nothing (figures, rows, lists), the website lists instances only to signed-in players |
| Probing a block | requests and invites answer the same with or without a block; the incoming cap never answers a sender (a request beyond it waits, 19.11) |
| Staff abuse | the role from the database, every action and look audited, playing staff tagged, blocks passed only by an audited moderation action; a report about a staff member is handled by another one and never shows him who reported him (19.25 "Round I1b") |
| A modified host client writes into guests' stories through the mirror | the mirror copies only what the guest's own STORY of the same visit also reported (19.8.6) |
| A removed guest's modified client keeps sending STORY | its owner switches at the removal, its stage group is detached (19.6.6) |
| Cheated characters among strangers | the Cheats tab fix before round I1 (19.25); round D's server character later; *Report player* from round I1b |
| Old clients | the protocol at `/status`, the relay's `ERR protocol` with a floor in code equal to the newest released protocol (49 since 0.1.7, 50 since 0.2.0, round I1b), 410 on `/rooms*` (19.18) |
| Free text | none anywhere; quick chat (I6) uses fixed phrases; reports pick a reason from a fixed list |

### 19.17 Server

#### 19.17.1 Database

Two migrations, numbers fixed at the integration (0011 is round 59's):
**00NN `friends`** with round I2's social lane, which runs beside round J
before round I1 (19.25): `friendships`, `friend_requests`,
`account_blocks` (built as `0012_friends`, with `cancelled_at` and without
the views, 19.25 "Round I2-social"); and **00NN+1 `world`** with round I1: `online_prefs`,
`instance_history` and its members, `player_reports` (I1b), the columns
and the views. Readable in HeidiSQL: names as the UI names things, enums as
text, no blobs, views with user names.

```sql
-- 00NN friends (round I2's social lane, before I1) -----------------------
CREATE TABLE friendships (                  -- one row per pair, account_lo < account_hi
  account_lo BIGINT UNSIGNED NOT NULL,
  account_hi BIGINT UNSIGNED NOT NULL,
  created_at DATETIME(3) NOT NULL,
  PRIMARY KEY (account_lo, account_hi),
  KEY ix_friendships_hi (account_hi),
  CONSTRAINT ck_friendships_order CHECK (account_lo < account_hi),
  CONSTRAINT fk_friendships_lo FOREIGN KEY (account_lo) REFERENCES accounts(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  CONSTRAINT fk_friendships_hi FOREIGN KEY (account_hi) REFERENCES accounts(id) ON DELETE CASCADE);

CREATE TABLE friend_requests (              -- accept deletes the row and writes friendships; cancel deletes it
  from_account_id BIGINT UNSIGNED NOT NULL,
  to_account_id   BIGINT UNSIGNED NOT NULL,
  state      ENUM('pending','declined') NOT NULL DEFAULT 'pending',  -- declined: shown "sent" to the sender until it expires
  delivered  TINYINT(1) NOT NULL DEFAULT 1, -- 0: not shown to the receiver: he blocks the sender, or it waits for a place (19.11)
  created_at DATETIME(3) NOT NULL,          -- pending and declined expire after Friends:RequestDays (30), then purged
  decided_at DATETIME(3) NULL,
  cancelled_at DATETIME(3) NULL,            -- (built) declined rows only: the sender cancelled it; hidden from him, the decline holds
  PRIMARY KEY (from_account_id, to_account_id),
  KEY ix_friend_requests_to (to_account_id, state, created_at),
  CONSTRAINT fk_fr_from FOREIGN KEY (from_account_id) REFERENCES accounts(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  CONSTRAINT fk_fr_to   FOREIGN KEY (to_account_id)   REFERENCES accounts(id) ON DELETE CASCADE);

CREATE TABLE account_blocks (
  account_id         BIGINT UNSIGNED NOT NULL,
  blocked_account_id BIGINT UNSIGNED NOT NULL,
  created_at         DATETIME(3) NOT NULL,
  PRIMARY KEY (account_id, blocked_account_id),
  KEY ix_blocks_blocked (blocked_account_id),
  CONSTRAINT fk_blocks_a FOREIGN KEY (account_id)         REFERENCES accounts(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  CONSTRAINT fk_blocks_b FOREIGN KEY (blocked_account_id) REFERENCES accounts(id) ON DELETE CASCADE);

-- 00NN+1 world (round I1) ------------------------------------------------
CREATE TABLE online_prefs (                 -- a missing row = the defaults
  account_id         BIGINT UNSIGNED NOT NULL PRIMARY KEY,

  invites            ENUM('anyone','friends') NOT NULL DEFAULT 'anyone',            -- Q11
  whereabouts        ENUM('friends','nobody') NOT NULL DEFAULT 'friends',
  friend_toasts      TINYINT(1) NOT NULL DEFAULT 1,

  light_mode         TINYINT UNSIGNED NOT NULL DEFAULT 1,  -- as RoomSettings.Default (LightMode 1)

CREATE TABLE instance_history (             -- written off the relay's lock through a queue; kept 90 days
  id              BIGINT UNSIGNED NOT NULL AUTO_INCREMENT PRIMARY KEY,  -- the history id; never the relay's wid (19.17.2)

  host_box        TINYINT UNSIGNED NOT NULL,     -- 1 until round D

ALTER TABLE speedrun_times      ADD COLUMN instance_id BIGINT UNSIGNED NULL AFTER room_id;

  MODIFY reason ENUM('room','reset','admin_restore','session','mirror') NOT NULL;

  -- as opening a room does today); 'mirror' 19.8.6 (no 'migration': question 36 (b), 19.22)
```

**Account deletion.** `AccountRepository.ScrubAsync` does not delete the
account row (it sets `status = 'deleted'` and an anonymous name) and
clears the owned tables by `WHERE account_id = @id`, so `ON DELETE CASCADE`
never fires and the new tables need their own statements, in the same
release as each migration: `friendships` (`account_lo` or `account_hi`),
`friend_requests` (`from_account_id` or `to_account_id`),
`account_blocks` (`account_id` or `blocked_account_id`), `online_prefs`,
`instance_history_members` (`account_id`), `player_reports` (as reporter;
reports about the account keep the anonymous id for staff). Hosted
`instance_history` rows keep the id, which now names the anonymous account.
`room_members` leaves the scrub list in the same release as the cleanup
migration that drops it (19.22 step 3); a scrub test per release
(`AccountScrubTests`: a deleted account with friends, requests both ways,
blocks both ways, history and reports is nobody's friend or blocker
afterwards, and the scrub runs without an error on the schema of that
release).

- `instance_history` and its members feed the admin pages, round D's
  `online_visits` (each row gets the instance and its host) and "Recently
  played with" (19.26).
- `audit_log` takes the events `instance_visibility`, `instance_remove`,
  `staff_join`, `staff_join_override`, `staff_spectate_start`,
  `staff_spectate_end`, `staff_end_instance`, `staff_remove`,
  `report_handled`. Friend and block changes are not audited (the tables
  are the record; refusals by the limits are logged). The details name
  other accounts by id (`hostId`, `memberIds`), never by name: an
  account's deletion renames its row, so no deleted player's name stays
  in other accounts' audit rows; the staff audit list shows the current
  names (`accounts`: "host Kim; members Kim, Lee"; I1a review).
- `rooms` and `room_members` lose their writer and stay read-only for one
  release; a cleanup migration drops them (19.22).
- Live state stays in the relay's memory: instances, stage groups, seats,
  parties, invites, presence selections.

#### 19.17.2 Runtime (relay memory)

| Object | Fields |
| --- | --- |
| `HubMember` (widened) | member id, account id, name, role, bound box, connection, its stage group and slot, its instance, party, friends and blocks (both directions, ids), prefs, presence (stage, last PRESENCE2), RTT samples, preferred slot, held seat, a go-along request (`GoAlong`: offer, stage, point, waiting or stamped, since when; round 72) |
| `WorldInstance` (new) | `wid` (u32, run-local, the only id on the wire; it may repeat after a restart), `HistoryId` (filled when the queued `instance_history` row is written; never sent to clients; the server maps `wid` to it for `achievement_unlocks.instance_id`, reports and the website), host member and box, data hash, visibility, settings and their hash, seats by member (taken, held, reserved), spectators, removal bars (account until time), host grace or return deadline, held story values, its stage groups, flags (starting, ending); round 72: its area, the visited stages, the go-along offers (at most three, 19.30.9) |
| `HubInstance` (the stage group, today) | plus its `WorldInstance` |
| `Party` | id, leader, members in join order, open invites (to, from, expires) |
| `Seat` | account, instance, until |
| Indexes | stage cells (19.17.4); members by account; instances by host; instances by area and data hash (round 72, the area candidates); the browser snapshot |

**The social cache.** The friends and blocks of a member are loaded when it
enters the world, outside the hub's lock (the admission does it before the
member is added). API and relay run in one process (`ServerApp`), so the
domain services tell the hub through an in-process `IWorldNotifier`
(`FriendsChanged(a, b, otherSees)`, `BlocksChanged(a, b)`, `PrefsChanged(a)`,
`AccountChanged(a)`, `StoryReplaced(a, box)`): no database read under the
hub's lock, no polling. Round I2's social lane, which runs before round I1,
ships the interface with a no-op implementation; round I1's relay
implements it. `FriendsChanged` says who may learn of the change (the
integration r71 review): `a` always, `b` only with `otherSees`; a decline
and the delivery of a waiting request are the receiver's alone (their
sender never learns of them, not even by a changed list or count), an
accept, a cancelled delivered request and a removed friend show on both
sides; the relay follows the flag and does not rebuild the rule from the
database.

**`WorldService`** (round I1, the facade that takes over `RoomService`'s
remaining jobs): `Counts` for the home page (`Index.cshtml.cs`'s
`CountsAsync`) and the admin index, from the browser snapshot;
`PlayContext(account)` for the achievements (19.8.9); account deletion,
lock and ban (`AccountEndpoints`, `AdminEndpoints`, the web's Account and
Admin pages) through `AccountChanged`; the story reset and restore through
`StoryReplaced` (19.8.1); `/admin/instances` and its actions. `RoomService`
keeps only `CloseLeftoversAsync` for the migration's start and goes with
the cleanup release.

**The browser snapshot.** Rebuilt every housekeeping pass (250 ms) as
immutable rows; OPTIONS, BROWSE, `GET /instances` and the friends'
whereabouts read it without the lock and filter per viewer (Visible() at
the decision stays under the lock).

#### 19.17.3 Admission, member ids, roles

- `POST /api/v1/world/enter` (token; the version gate; maintenance; the
  account's status; rate-limited like today's room join) answers with a
  one-time relay ticket (HMAC, 60 s; claims account, role, nonce; no room),
  the relay port, the account's prefs and settings, its bound box and its
  held seat (I5).
- **One world session per account.** A second *enter* (another PC) replaces
  the first: the old connection gets CLOSE *replaced* ("Signed in on another
  PC"), round 59's `await_hello` order kept. This also keeps one keeper per
  (account, box) in one place. The replaced client does not reconnect by
  itself (CLOSE *replaced* turns its automatic reconnect off). A replaced
  **host** ends his instance at once (END `host_left`, the guests' 3 s
  notice): the new PC starts at the title, has no engine in that instance
  and could not resume it, so a grace would only make the guests wait 60 s
  for nothing.
- **Handshake** unchanged in form: `DW4R2 <ticket> <protocol> <dataHash> 0`
  (the settings hash field stays and is ignored), answered `OK <memberId>
  <serverTimeMs>` or `ERR protocol | data | ticket | full | busy | banned`.
- **The protocol floor in code.** `Play:MinimumProtocol` is a configuration
  value (48 in `deploy/appsettings.Production.example.json` after
  integration r71; `VersionGate` compares against it), so a forgotten edit
  would let a 48 client past the version gate to a generic 410 on `/rooms`. The world therefore refuses
  below round I1's protocol (49, or the next free number at I1's
  integration, 19.18) whatever the configuration: `VersionGate` uses
  `max(Play:MinimumProtocol, Wire.WorldProtocol)` and the relay answers
  `ERR protocol` below that constant, the same one the handshake checks,
  so the floor never falls behind the protocol (a floor of 47 would admit
  today's room clients, which speak 48). DEPLOY.md's step still raises the configured
  value (19.22 step 7; the production example says 49), and W22 runs
  against a server that kept 48 (an update without that step).
- **The data hash.** Today the room join compares the client's data hash
  with the room creator's (`RoomService`, `room.DataHash != dataHash`), and
  "ranked" means that hash is in `Rooms:RankedDataHashes`. In the world: `World:DataHashes` (a
  list; empty = any) is checked at the handshake (`ERR data`, "Your game
  data is not supported on this server"); each member's hash rides on the
  member, a stage group and an instance carry their host's, and the data
  hash is a **matching filter**: candidates, co-arrivals, travels and the
  browser show only instances with the viewer's hash (19.7.2), so engines
  with different game data never share a stage group. "Ranked" is per
  instance: its hash is in `RankedDataHashes` (the achievements' context,
  19.8.9).
- **Member ids.** A u32 given to an account at its first admission in a
  server run; it stays while the account is online or holds a seat and is
  never reused in the run. It replaces the room index everywhere on the
  wire. Names come with MEMBER_INFO before a member is first mentioned to a
  receiver; account ids never go on the wire.
- **Roles** in the ticket from the database, re-checked live (19.14).

#### 19.17.4 One hub, stage cells and the load gate

- **One hub.** `RelayHub._rooms` holds a single hub for the world: today's
  `RoomHub` keeps its barriers, sealing, forks, holds, story, presence and
  state budget code and its lock (`Sync`). It is not renamed in round I1, so
  round J's relay lane merges cleanly; the world layer goes into new files
  (`World/WorldInstance.cs`, `World/Matching.cs`, `World/Social.cs`,
  `World/Presence.cs`) with targeted edits in `Decide`, `JoinOrNew`,
  `FanPresence`, `OnStory` and `Connect`. A rename to `WorldHub` waits for a
  quiet round.
- **Stage cells.** The flat collections (`_members`, `_instances`, `_holds`)
  get an index by stage: a cell holds every stage group of that stage, the
  holds for it (co-arrival bases, prompts, join holds, boss holds) and, for
  hub stages, the occupants for presence. Every decision of 3.4 and 19.7
  reads one cell (`Decide`, `JoinOrNew`, the co-arrival search, the
  candidates, the boss lock); a barrier moves its members from the cell of
  the old stage to the cell of the target. Round 72's area candidates
  (19.30.3) read the index of instances by area and data hash besides the
  arrival stage's cell (at most `World:MaxInstances` rows, microseconds
  under the lock); go-along offers change only at barrier decisions and
  INTENTs (19.30.9).
- **Phase 1: one lock** for everything, measured. Expected work per second
  for 200 members (estimates; round I1 measures them):

  | Path | Rate | Notes |
  | --- | --- | --- |
  | INPUT received | 120 sealed members x 60 | as in a room |
  | SEALED built and sent | 30 sealed stage groups x 60 | `SealOne`, microseconds |
  | PRESENCE2 fan-out | 60 lobby members x 10 | at most 30 receivers' selections per sender (today every room member) |
  | PING, NETSTAT, NETFP, INSTANCE_INFO | 1 per member | INSTANCE_INFO only to the own instance |
  | Barrier decisions | a few per second | one cell each |
  | State builds | rare | already off the lock (`StateJob`) |

- **The load gate** (round I1a's first relay task): the existing C# fake
  clients, 200 members: 120 in 30 sealed stage groups of four, 20 solo-led
  in fields, 60 in stagML11 sending PRESENCE2 at 10 Hz, one barrier a second
  somewhere, BROWSE once a second from ten of them. Measured: the lock's
  hold time p50 / p99 / max, the sealing lateness (a SEALED's due time
  against its send) p99, the sealing thread's failed `TryEnter`s (every
  INPUT and PRESENCE2 takes `hub.Sync`, and a miss there is world-wide seal
  jitter), CPU and memory. Further cells, each a pass of its own:
  - **a full hub:** 200 members in stagML11 sending PRESENCE2 at 10 Hz (the
    selection and fan-out at its worst);
  - **joins with states:** 10 joins a minute into sealed stage groups with
    state builds (`MaxConcurrentStateBuilds` is 2 relay-wide and
    `FinishState` runs under the lock), plus STORY merges and mirrors at
    every barrier;
  - **a reconnect storm:** 200 reconnects within 10 s (a router restart),
    with each keeper and social cache loaded outside the lock.

  **Pass** in every cell: hold p99 at most 0.5 ms and max at most 5 ms,
  sealing lateness p99 at most 2 ms, the relay under half a core on the
  reference machine (a full core in the storm cell, for its 10 s). A pass
  keeps phase 1; the numbers go into this section.

  **Measured r71 (redone after the review).** The first runs of this
  section are void: the harness sent the lobby's growing phase as the yaw,
  past `PresenceMsg.MaxYaw` (4 pi) after 12-25 s, and the hub dropped
  27,406 of 60,008 PRESENCE2 in *fullhub* (46 %) as implausible, so every
  fan-out, hold and CPU figure of the presence was about half the real one.
  The harness now sends the yaw in -pi..pi (`LoadGate.LobbyPresence`; a test
  sends five minutes of it through a hub) and marks a run invalid, exiting
  1, when the hub dropped any presence as implausible, more than 1 % for the
  presence bucket, or refused a frame (`LoadGate.InvalidReasons`); every run
  below is valid. Two harnesses, `DW4Online.FakeClient`
  (`tests/DW4Online.FakeClient/LoadGate.cs`, `LoadGateNet.cs`), the same
  cells and rates (a sealed member's INPUT every tick, three ticks ahead at
  most, NETFP every 60th tick once sealed, one STATE after the load; a solo
  leader's LOG every 100 ms and STATE every second; a lobby member's
  PRESENCE2 at 10 Hz; one solo barrier a second with its snapshot; the
  browser's `Views()` ten times a second), server GC as the service
  (`DOTNET_gcServer=1`), 3 s warm-up, 30 s measured (60 s for *joins*),
  Ryzen 7 7800X3D with other rounds running beside it:
  - `loadgate` **in-process**: today's `RoomHub` (one lock) holding all 200
    members without sockets; eight worker threads call `Receive` under
    `hub.Sync`; the lock's holds per path are timed. The sealing thread as
    `RelayHub.SealRoom` (`TryEnter`, a retry a millisecond later), the
    housekeeping every 250 ms as `RelayHub.HousekeepAsync`. *fullhub* fans
    every PRESENCE2 out to all 199 others (today's loop); *select* splits
    the 200 into seven presence stages (about 29 receivers each) and
    computes a prototype of the selection (for each receiver the nearest 30,
    once a second) under the lock; *joins* is the base load with 15 of the
    30 groups at three members and ten joins a minute of lobby members into
    them (BARRIER, the state built off the lock, `FinishState`, READY, the
    JOIN stamped; the joiner then sends INPUT).
  - `loadgate --sockets`: the real relay (`RelayHub` with its connections'
    read and write loops, `SealLoop`, the housekeeping and `Views`) in a
    child process on loopback, the 200 members as lean fake clients, one TCP
    connection each, in the measuring process. Measured in the relay
    process: its CPU (with the sends), `RelayHub.SealPasses` /
    `SealTryMisses` and `RoomHub.SealLateness` (new diagnostics of the
    relay: per instance pass, the time of the pass with the lock held
    against the due time of its first due tick). Not the joins cell (in-
    process only).

  Logs (worktree `i1ameas`): `build/meas2/loadgate_r1.json`,
  `loadgate_net_r1.json`, `joins_r1.json`, `gate_r1.log`, the summary
  `lg_table2.py`; the experiment below `loadgate_net_batch_r1.json`; the
  void first runs `build/meas/loadgate2.json`, `loadgate3_nomargin.json`,
  `joins2.json`.

  In-process (holds of `hub.Sync`):

  | Cell | Acquisitions | Hold p50 / p99 / p99.9 / p99.99 / max | Sealing lateness p50 / p99 / max | TryEnter misses | CPU | Working set |
  | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
  | base (30x4 sealed, 20 solo, 60 lobby) | 8,522/s | 0.2 µs / 12.0 µs / 0.06 / 2.9 / **64.2 ms** | 0.38 / **4.81** / 58.0 ms | 82.5/s of 402 passes | 0.06 cores | 91 MB |
  | fullhub (200 in stagML11, today's fan-out) | 2,034/s | 4.9 µs / 17.6 µs / 0.12 / 0.39 / 0.82 ms | - | - | 0.02 | 87 MB |
  | select (seven presence stages, the selection prototype) | 2,035/s | 5.1 µs / 14.7 µs / 0.18 / 0.77 / 3.37 ms | - | - | 0.03 | 80 MB |
  | storm (base, 200 reconnects in 10 s) | 8,392/s | 0.2 µs / 21.3 µs / 0.07 / 1.9 / **8.8 ms** | 0.58 / **5.30** / 12.5 ms | 108.6/s of 310 | 0.09 | 97 MB |
  | sealonly (the 30 groups alone) | 7,567/s | 0.2 µs / 16.1 µs / 0.05 / 2.5 / **15.9 ms** | 0.35 / **4.42** / 16.9 ms | 59.7/s of 285 | 0.04 | 104 MB |
  | base, the sealer waits up to 2 ms | 8,401/s | 0.2 µs / 20.0 µs / 0.06 / 2.1 / **10.5 ms** | 0.23 / 0.50 / 10.9 ms | 0 | 0.06 | 106 MB |
  | storm, the sealer waits up to 2 ms | 8,387/s | 0.2 µs / 22.8 µs / 0.06 / 2.3 / **8.0 ms** | 0.23 / 0.52 / 8.4 ms | 0 | 0.07 | 103 MB |
  | joins (base load, 15 groups of three, 10 joins in 60 s) | 7,832/s | 0.2 µs / 21.7 µs / 0.07 / 3.2 / **17.3 ms** | 0.30 / **4.78** / 19.4 ms | 30/s of 203 | 0.06 | 115 MB |

  The lock is busy 1.1-1.8 % of the time in every cell. Per path (base):
  INPUT p99 0.6 µs (215,027 in 30 s), PRESENCE2 to the 59 others 8.8 µs,
  LOG 8.5 µs, a solo barrier 0.14-0.26 ms, `Views()` 31 µs (p99 70 µs),
  `Seal` 46 µs p99 (max 8.5 ms), the housekeeping 94 µs p50 and 7.5-21 ms
  p99 in every cell with sealed groups (max 64 ms once in base); fullhub's
  PRESENCE2 to 199 others 12.5 µs p99; the storm's Connect 37 µs p50 /
  64 µs p99, Disconnect 25 / 86 µs, RESUME 2 / 11 µs. The fan-out the hub
  does: *base* 43,112 frames a second (59 KB/s to each lobby member);
  *fullhub* 398,538 (28.2 MB/s, **141 KB/s per receiver**); *select*
  55,700 (4.6 MB/s, **23 KB/s per receiver**, 82 bytes a frame: every one
  of about 28 others at 10 Hz). The selection as 19.13 designs it (the
  nearest 10 at 10 Hz, 20 more at 5 Hz: 200 frames a second) is about
  16 KB/s per receiver at these frames, against the estimate of 12 KB/s.

  The joins under the base load (*joins*): all ten joined; from the
  joiner's BARRIER to its state complete 15.3-15.6 ms, to the JOIN stamped
  15.4-21.7 ms; the joiner's BARRIER held the lock 0.11 ms p50 (8.1 ms
  max), READY 0.08 ms p50 (6.2 ms max), `FinishState` at most 0.024 ms,
  the builds off the lock 0.17-0.26 ms (373 KB of state in all). The joins
  on an idle hub (`joins`, the log length's effect, `joins_r1.json`): the
  joiner's BARRIER 0.03-0.06 ms (the refused one 0.64 ms), `FinishState` 0.03-0.11 ms classic and
  0.39-0.77 ms from a checkpoint, READY and JOIN_AT under 0.01 ms, a
  checkpoint's 32 KB chunk at most 0.90 ms, the build off the lock
  0.6-7.9 ms (51 KB of state after a minute, 310 KB after ten, a
  checkpoint's 1.1 MB), and a LOG of 1,200 pads 0.45-0.59 ms p50 and up to
  5.3 ms (one such LOG in the first checkpoint run, in the first runs too).
  After 25 minutes the classic join is refused: its BARRIER_OK is NEW with
  the notice *TooLongToCatchUp* (89,910 ticks at the default replay rate of
  3,000 is a 30.6 s catch-up, `Instances:MaxCatchUpSeconds` 30); the
  checkpoint path joins.

  Over sockets (the real relay):

  | Cell | Relay CPU | Clients' CPU | Sealing passes | TryEnter misses | Sealing lateness: share over 1 / 2 / 5 ms | Frames to the clients |
  | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
  | base | **0.72** (again: 0.85) cores | 0.52 | 1,098/s | 7.6/s (0.7 %) | 1.2 / 0.50 / 0.15 % | 43,128/s, 3.5 MB/s |
  | fullhub | **4.01** | 2.15 | - | - | - | 398,612/s, 28.2 MB/s |
  | select | **0.66** | 0.42 | - | - | - | 55,709/s, 4.6 MB/s |
  | storm | 0.98 (again: 0.88) | 0.63 | 989/s | 10.6/s (1.1 %) | 1.8 / 0.68 / 0.27 % | 47,094/s; 200 reconnects, 120 RESUMEs |
  | sealonly | 0.39 | 0.26 | 1,032/s | 5.0/s (0.5 %) | 0.7 / 0.35 / 0.12 % | 7,505/s |

  ("again": the cells *base-wait* and *storm-wait*, which over sockets are
  *base* and *storm* once more: the real relay has no wait.)

  What fails, and why:
  1. **The housekeeping's ping pass** holds the lock 7.5-21 ms once a
     second (the p99 of the housekeeping holds in every cell with sealed
     groups): for every sealed member it sends PING with the delay rule's
     low margin, `DelayController.LowMargin()` (`RoomHub.cs` 2640), which
     copies and sorts the stream's whole fall window, up to 1,800 margins
     (`SlotStream.cs` 299-319); with 120 sealed members 120 sorts a second.
     A room had at most ten members, so it never showed. The first runs
     measured the pass without the margin at all (an experiment, not
     committed; the lower bound of a cheaper margin, not an incremental
     one): housekeeping p99 1.3-1.7 ms.
  2. **The sealing thread's `TryEnter` misses** in-process (15-35 % of the
     passes) come from the harness, as the review suspected: its worker
     threads and the sealing thread all wake from high-resolution waitable
     timers, and 45-75 % of the sealing passes had a worker wake within
     2 µs (independent wakes at the workers' rate would give 0.75-2.5 %),
     57-92 % of the misses within 2 µs and 95-99 % within 10 µs
     (`wakes` in the JSON). Over sockets the real relay misses 0.5-1.1 % of
     its passes, close to the lock's busy share, and its sealing lateness
     p99 is under 2 ms in every cell (over 2 ms: 0.35-0.68 % of the passes):
     **the sealing passes the gate with `TryEnter` as built**.
  3. **The max of 5 ms fails** in every cell with sealed groups: single
     holds of 8-64 ms (the ping pass, `Seal` up to 15.9 ms, a solo barrier
     up to 17.3 ms), at p99.99 1.9-3.2 ms. Some of them are the server
     GC's pauses (20-72 collections in a window) and the machine's other
     work (other rounds ran beside every run); they were not separated.
  4. **The relay's CPU fails** in *base* (0.72-0.85 cores) and *select*
     (0.66), *fullhub* takes 4 cores, *storm* stays under its full core
     (0.88-0.98), *sealonly* under half (0.39). The lock's own work is
     0.02-0.09 cores (in-process), so the cost is the connection path:
     one socket write per frame (`Connection.WriteLoopAsync`) and two reads
     per frame (header and payload, `ReadLoopAsync`) on the thread pool,
     about 10-26 µs of CPU per frame in and out. An experiment (not
     committed; the patch is `build/meas2/connection_batch_experiment.patch`):
     the queued frames coalesced into one write and the reads buffered gave
     0.74 (base), 1.04 (select), 3.1 (fullhub) and 0.45 (sealonly) cores,
     nothing measurable (the frames reach a connection one at a time; the
     runs spread by about a third on the busy machine, the clients' process
     took 0.26-2.2 cores beside the relay).

  **Verdict, provisional:** phase 1 does not pass the gate as designed
  (the criteria stay as written above): the holds' p99 (12-23 µs) and the
  sealing lateness p99 over sockets (under 2 ms) pass; the max of 5 ms
  fails in every cell with sealed groups and the relay's CPU in *base* and
  *select*. The lock is busy 1.1-1.8 %, so none of the failures is the
  lock's contention, and phase 2 (a lock per cell) would fix none of them.
  **Design changes (r71, revised after the review), phase 1 kept
  provisionally:** (a) the margin PING carries is computed incrementally or
  cached per stream (the delay rule's own `Evaluate` every 60 ticks may
  keep it), never sorted per PING; (b) *withdrawn*: the sealing thread
  keeps `TryEnter` (the first runs' "wait up to 2 ms" answered the
  harness's timers, not the relay); `RelayHub.SealRoom` counts its misses
  and reads the pass's time once the lock is held (any later wait for the
  lock seals with a fresh time), `RoomHub.SealLateness` records the
  lateness (both built in this round, with tests); (c) the presence
  selection is computed off the lock from an immutable copy of the
  positions (built in housekeeping, as the browser snapshot) and only
  swapped in under it (the prototype under the lock: 0.54 ms p50, 3.4 ms
  max); (d) the fan-out by selection stays (19.13): without it a lobby of
  200 sends 141 KB/s to every member and takes 4 relay cores; (e) *new*:
  the relay lane measures and cuts the connection path's CPU per frame
  before the world opens (coalescing alone did not). Then the gate runs
  again with `loadgate --sockets` and in-process, all cells, on a quiet
  machine, criteria as below; it decides phase 1 or 2. The user
  decided on 2026-11-05 (section 18, question 42) that the max is read at
  p99.99 when a busy machine's single pauses are the only holds over 5 ms:
  the hold criterion is "p99 at most 0.5 ms and p99.99 at most 5 ms", which
  every in-process cell above meets (p99.99 1.9-3.2 ms). The relay's CPU over
  sockets is open either way (e). Not
  measured: STORY merges and mirrors at barriers (the keepers per account
  and the mirror come with I1a's story lane), joins over sockets (the
  in-process joins cell only), an incremental margin and the selection off
  the lock (only after (a) and (c) are built), TLS (the relay has none).

`Instances:CoArrivalHoldMs`, `JoinHoldSeconds`, `MaxCatchUpSeconds`,
`JoinRequestTries` and round J's keys stay. `Rooms:*` (among them
`StoryWhileOwnerAway`) is ignored with one log warning and removed in the
cleanup; `Rooms:RankedDataHashes` is read as `World:RankedDataHashes` for
one release, `Play:RequireRoom` as `Play:RequireWorld`. `Play:MinimumProtocol`
stays, with the floor in code (I1's protocol, 19.17.3).

**Log memory.** A sealed visit's log costs about 1.6 KB per second (four
6-byte pads plus events per tick at 59.94 Hz), about 5.8 MB per hour;
`Instances:MaxVisitHours` (12) caps one visit near 70 MB. A room's ten
members bounded the sum, a world does not: above `World:LogBudgetMB` the
longest visits stop taking classic joins (as `LogFull` today); after round
J a visit keeps only the log after its newest agreed checkpoint and takes
joins from checkpoints only. Hub stage groups log nothing.

### 19.18 Protocol

The protocol rises to the next free number when round I1 is integrated:
at least **49**, since round J's READY check took 48 (`kOnlineProtocol` in
`online_run.hpp`, `Wire.ReadyCheckProtocol`); written 49 below. The floor
in code (19.17.3) is that number itself, one constant per side. Message numbers
follow the registry of 6.3 after round J (J holds client 0x15-0x17 and server
0x92-0x93, 6.13.7; server 0x91 is free) and are pinned at the integration;
golden vectors on both sides (`online_wire_tests.cpp`,
`WireGoldenTests.cs`) and the registry checks as always.

**New, client to server:**

| Type | Message | Fields | When |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 0x18 | PLAN | plan id u16, purpose (gate, board, other), stage, point, context hash, group size | the gate form, while the confirming press is held (19.7.4); at most one a second per member |
| 0x19 | CHOICE | plan id or (inst, visit), choice (1 join, 2 new, 3 back, 4 travel row, 5 return: a defeated host's *Return*), wid, visibility, flags (wait at a boss lock) | the prompt's answer: with HEADING (gate form) or at the held barrier (loading-screen form, the return hold); 3 at a held barrier from home = the redirect back (19.7.5) |
| 0x1A | GOTO | request id, mode (1 join instance, 2 join friend, 3 party follow, 4 go to host, 5 seat rejoin, 6 spectate, 7 join as moderator, 8 go to member: round 72), target (wid or member id) | browser, friend list, party, Online menu, reconnect (I3, I5); modes 4 and 8 inside the own instance stamp GO (19.9.6) |
| 0x1B | INSTANCE_OP | op (1 visibility, 2 remove member, 3 end: host or staff), argument | the host, staff |
| 0x1E | REPORT | member, reason (fixed list), wid or 0 | *Report player* (I1b); `Reports:PerDay` |
| 0x1C | BROWSE | filter (all, party and friends, area), area, page | the browser; at most one a second |
| 0x1D | PARTY_OP | op (invite, accept, decline, leave, promote, remove, follow answer, gather), member or account | I4 |

**New, server to client:**

| Type | Message | Fields | When |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 0x91 | OPTIONS | plan id or (inst, visit), stage, remembered visibility, preselected row (or *New instance*, decision 40), rows: wid, host member and name, relation flags (party, friend host, friends inside), the host's stage (round 72), players, players at the arrival stage (round 72), seats (taken, held, reserved), story label, same story point, difficulty, settings flags (randomizer, other settings), state (joinable, boss fight, loading, host away, full, arriving now, other quest, story not here yet), visibility (staff only), worst round trip ms | the answer to PLAN; at a held barrier; again on change, at most once a second |
| 0x94 | INSTANCE_LIST | page, total, rows as OPTIONS plus area, stage and age | the answer to BROWSE |
| 0x95 | INSTANCE_INFO | wid, host member, visibility, settings, story label, members (member, slot, stage, level, flags connected / lagging / staff), seats, grace seconds left, own role (host, guest, staff, spectator) | on change (the Online menu, the status line, the lag icons) |
| 0x96 | WORLD_NOTICE | kind, member, name, argument | joined, left, went to a stage, visibility changed, removed, host away (seconds), host back, ended (reason), lagging, lag over, shared progress saved, friend online / offline / request / accepted, invite, party joined / left / leader / heading, go refused (round 72: the reason, offer closed or the member moved), report (14, round I1b), apart (15, round I1b's integration: the member left the receiver's stage group but keeps its seat, a lag LEAVE or a split barrier) |
| 0x97 | MEMBER_INFO | member, name, level, flags (friend, party, staff tag) | before a member's first mention to this receiver; on a relation change |
| 0x98 | FRIENDS_STATE | online friends: member, name, area, stage, wid, flags (host, joinable for this viewer, private, hidden) | on change, at most once per 2 s per friend (I2) |
| 0x99 | GOTO_RESULT | request id, result (ok, boss wait, full, not found, ended, removed, busy, other settings, too long), stage, token (0 for a GOTO inside the own instance, 19.9.6), seconds | the answer to GOTO |
| 0x9A | PARTY_STATE | party, leader, members (member, name, area, wid, connected), open invite | I4, on change |
| 0x9B | OFFER | offer id u16, op (1 open, 2 changed, 3 closed), flags (show the notice), entrants (count u8, member u32 each), stage (where the first entrant is), notice seconds u8, close reason (left, defeated, ended, gone along) | round 72 (I1b, 19.30.5): to the members a go-along offer concerns, when it opens, gains an entrant (the notice again), moves deeper (no notice) or closes; to a member arriving in a field while one is open (with the notice only as a late notice, 19.30.5; never for a member that was in a dungeon when it opened) |

**Changed:**

- WELCOME 0x80: the member as u32; flags world, seat held, staff; the seat's
  wid. A RESUME or WELCOME that does not name the client's instance tells
  it the instance is gone (19.6.10).
- RESUME (client): + the stage and visit the client's engine continues, so
  a guest that continues alone is filed at its stage (19.15).
- CLOSE: + the reason *replaced* turns the client's automatic reconnect off
  (19.17.3).
- HEADING 0x03 (round 72): + asked u8, the slots the exit port asked on
  the mat for this departure that stay (`ExitPort::asked` without the
  leavers): no go-along notice for them (19.30.5). The relay resolves them
  to member ids when HEADING arrives, against the stage group the port ran
  in (an exit fork's parent when the sender is in its child already).
- BARRIER 0x04: + travel token u32 (0: none), + plan id u16.
- BARRIER_OK 0x84: members as u32 in the co-arrival list; + wid, host
  member, settings and their hash, the story owner key, the story mode
  (merge, replace), a redirect stage and point for a DISSOLVE; decision 5
  SPECTATE (I3). The dropped set goes. Round 72: the mode *replace* with
  the host's story, owner key and settings also for a guest's NEW
  (19.30.4).
- BARRIER_WAIT 0x85: the reasons *choice* (OPTIONS follows), *host away*
  and *return* (a defeated host's 60 s, I3).
- JOIN_REQ 0x83: + kind (join, home, go) for solo-led stage groups
  (19.6.5); *go* (round 72) with the stage and point (19.30.7).
- INTENT 0x0D: kind 3 *leave* (the own slot home; the relay stamps HOME);
  kind 4 *go along* (round 72; argument: the offer id; 0 the player's
  *Cancel*; -1 the client's report that its stamped GO ended without a
  departure, expired or done nothing at its step; the relay holds it until
  the target is ready, then stamps GO, 19.30.7).
- STATE 0x0C (round 72, I1b): + flag 16 *no living member* (no present
  slot alive, from the engine's alive mask), sent at once like the boss
  lock: the go-along wait and every JOIN hold read it (no rescue joins,
  19.9.3, 19.30.7).
- STORY 0x0E / STORY_ACK 0x89: + the owner key (member u32, box u8); the
  next free reason *owner*; STORY also marks which of its values are in
  the sender's join base (I2, 19.8.6).
- PRESENCE 0x87 and PRESENCE2 0x90 to clients: the member as u32, relation
  flags.
- Tick events: JOIN + spawn kind (0xFF the entrance point, 0-3 next to that
  slot); HOME (slot mask, reason) is new and forks with `ForkKind::home`
  (exactly the mask, 19.6.5); GO (slot u8 first, point u8, stage) is new
  (round 72): applied like INTENT at the first membership-safe step, every
  GO of that step together (one `Engine::online_go` with their mask), the
  exit port's departure with an exit's side rule and the new fork kind
  `ForkKind::go` (forked between two steps like `give_up`, so its recorded
  side is one frame later than an exit's), the stage taken as named; a GO
  not applied 300 ticks after its tick expires on every engine (19.30.7).
  At a fork GO and HOME follow their slots as LEAVE, INTENT and DELAY do
  (`TickEvent.Slot` names GO's slot; HOME's mask is split by side), so a
  GO waiting behind a fork goes with its slot into the child. Their
  numbers follow round J's events and are pinned at the integration.
- ROOM 0x8A and ROSTER 0x8D retire; their numbers stay reserved for good.
- The client skips (and logs once) an undecodable WORLD_NOTICE,
  MEMBER_INFO, FRIENDS_STATE, INSTANCE_LIST, INSTANCE_INFO, PARTY_STATE or
  OFFER (an offer it cannot read is one it never answers);
  an undecodable OPTIONS means "nothing to choose" (NEW).

**Old clients.** The server's minimum protocol is round I1's (49), as a
floor in code
whatever `Play:MinimumProtocol` says (19.17.3): the version gate shows
"Update required" before any call, the relay answers `ERR protocol`,
`/rooms*` answers 410 `rooms_retired`. Rooms and the world cannot run side
by side, so server and client are deployed together, as with every protocol
rise. The direct `--host` / `--join` LAN sessions are untouched.

### 19.19 REST API (v1, HTTPS 8443)

| Method and path | Auth | What |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `POST /world/enter` | player | ticket, relay port, prefs and settings, bound box, held seat (19.17.3) |
| `POST /world/ticket` | player | a new ticket for a reconnect |
| `POST /world/leave` | player | ends the world session (the relay sends BYE) |
| `GET /world` | public | players online, instances per area; no names |
| `GET /instances?area=` | player | the instances visible to the caller (19.7.2); staff all |
| `GET /friends` | player | friends with presence, requests in and out, blocks |
| `POST /friends/requests {username}` | player | send (limits of 19.11) |
| `POST /friends/requests/{username}/accept`, `.../decline`, `DELETE /friends/requests/{username}` | player | answer, cancel |
| `DELETE /friends/{username}` | player | remove |
| `GET /blocks`, `POST /blocks {username}`, `DELETE /blocks/{username}` | player | blocks (19.11) |
| `GET /players/{username}` | player | the public card plus the relation to the caller |
| `GET /me/online-prefs`, `PUT /me/online-prefs` | player | 19.17.1 |
| `GET /admin/instances`, `POST /admin/instances/{id}/end?run=`, `POST /admin/instances/{id}/remove?run= {username}` | staff | audited; the listing names the relay's run (`WorldSnapshot.Run`), and End / Remove need it: wids count from 1 again after a restart (fix-019: 422 `run_required`, 409 `instance_list_outdated`) |
| `GET /admin/audit?event=` | staff | the staff rows (a moderator his own, an admin all) |
| `POST /reports {username, reason}` | player | *Report player* (I1b; the relay's REPORT goes to the same service) |
| `GET /admin/reports`, `POST /admin/reports/{id}/done` | staff | the report list; audited `report_handled` |
| `/rooms*` | - | 410 `rooms_retired` for one release |

### 19.20 Website

- **`/instances`** (replaces `/rooms`, which redirects): signed-in players
  see the instances open to them by area (host, stage, players x/4, story
  point, tags, age); signed-out visitors see counts per area only. Private
  instances never, except for staff.
- **Profiles `/u/{name}`** (9.1.12) get *Add friend* / *Request sent* /
  *Accept request* / *Friends* with *Remove*, *Block* / *Unblock*; online
  status, whereabouts and "last online" only for friends (by their
  preference).
- **`/account/friends`:** friends, requests in and out (accept, decline,
  cancel), blocks (unblock), the online preferences (default visibility,
  invites, whereabouts, toasts) and "Recently played with" (19.26).
- **Admin:** `/admin/instances` (every instance, Private included, with
  members, host, visibility, settings, age and spectators; *End*, *Remove*),
  `/admin/reports` (open reports with the instance they came from; *Done*)
  and the audit list; the admin account page shows the account's instance
  history and the reports about it. The home page's counts come from
  `WorldService` (19.17.2).
- **The privacy page** adds what friends see, what is public, that blocks
  are never revealed, and that moderators may watch any instance (logged).
- The navigation's *Rooms* becomes *Instances*.

### 19.22 Migration (round I1's deploy)

1. **Stories (Q14).** Nothing to convert: a room's story has always been
   its owner's own `online_story` row (8.4), and a guest's own story was
   never touched. The owner plays it as his own from round I1 on; round D's
   data step puts it into box 1. `online_story_history` keeps its rows
   (reason *room*).
2. **Players who were only guests** (question 36, the user's answer (b)).
   An account whose own story is empty starts at zero; nothing of a room's
   story is copied to it. The user rejected the copy (a) because it could
   be abused: join the room of a player near the end, and the copy finishes
   the game more or less at once. Any instance can be joined anyway (Q5),
   so such a player still plays with his friends from the first day. No
   data step and no history reason *migration*.
3. **Rooms.** The service start closes every open room as today
   (`CloseLeftoversAsync`, *server_restart*); `rooms` and `room_members`
   stay read-only; `/rooms*` answers 410. A cleanup migration one release
   later drops them, with `RoomService`, `RoomRepository` and
   `Rooms.cshtml` (it needs DEPLOY.md's DROP grant and a fresh backup); in
   the same release `room_members` leaves `AccountRepository.ScrubAsync`'s
   list, or every account deletion would fail (19.17.1).
4. **Settings.** Each owner's newest room settings fill his `online_prefs`
   (camera, light, fast loading, randomizer seed and modes); everyone else
   gets the defaults, which are `RoomSettings.Default`'s (camera 0, light 1,
   fast loading off), so a player's world plays as his rooms did. The
   difficulty is the box's (19.8.7).
5. **Accounts, characters, achievements, cloud backups** stay as they are.
   `achievement_unlocks` and `speedrun_times` keep `room_id` on old rows.
6. **Round D.** The `/play` binding (`online_play`, "one row per account and
   room") becomes one row per account and world session; the box switch
   stays possible only at the title (stagIS*).
7. **The user's steps** (DEPLOY.md gets them, with the HeidiSQL guide for the
   new tables and views): a database backup in HeidiSQL; in the server's
   `appsettings.Production.json` `Play:MinimumProtocol` set to 49 (I1's
   protocol; the code refuses below it anyway, 19.17.3) and `Play:RequireRoom` renamed
   `Play:RequireWorld`; the server release (it migrates at the start); the
   client release, both together. Rooms are gone after the update. Round
   I2's social migration (`friends`) comes earlier with its own release and
   needs only the backup.

### 19.23 Online off and determinism

New engine paths, all behind `Engine::online()`:

- the replace at DISSOLVE and `redirect_pending_stage` (a solo engine only);
- HOME (server-stamped, the home departure for a mask);
- the JOIN spawn next to a slot (the safe positions: a field of the online
  block, updated in every step, the same on every engine);
- `online_depart_home()` (a port departure, at home, where a solo hub
  instance is never joined or logged, and in a solo engine whose instance
  the relay no longer knows, which nobody can join or log either, 19.6.10;
  in a live instance the same departure comes as HOME, a stamped event, or
  in a solo-led stage group at the tick its leader names through JOIN_AT);
- `ForkKind::home` (exactly the mask leaves; the side rule stays for every
  other fork kind);
- GO (round 72: a stamped event in a live instance, or JOIN_AT's tick in a
  solo-led stage group; the exit port's departure for the GO slots of one
  step with an exit's side rule, forked as `ForkKind::go` between two
  steps, the target taken as named, expiring unapplied after 300 ticks,
  19.30.7);
- the replace at a guest's NEW (round 72: a solo engine from home, parked
  at its barrier before its transition steps, 19.30.4);
- the settings at a restore;
- help-mode carries;
- the spectator's observer engine.

The gate form's input hold changes no engine code: the engine sees a press
later. `pending_departure_choice()` reads only. The Cheats tab fix and the
half-rate ghost animation are UI and presentation.

Proof as always: `det.sh` 4004f056 / audio 396cb219 twice, r25c 10 of 10
with 1,748,011 frames, the save state suite 17 of 17.

**The harness** (`tools/online_test/run.py`) is room-based today: it
creates rooms (around lines 358-362), starts clients with
`--online-create` / `--online-join` (`game_main.cpp`) and reads
`room_<code>.jsonl` (around 480, 894, 1094). In the world every scenario
on one server would see the others (Public by default, prompts, ghosts),
and `DW4_ONLINE_AUTOCHOICE=first` could pick an instance a previous
scenario left behind. Round I1 has a harness lane: clients start with
`--online-play`; the relay writes its membership log per world run and
instance (`world_<run>.jsonl` with the `wid` on every line); and **each
scenario gets a fresh server process** with its own database (run.py's
`start_server` already does this for scenarios with their own settings;
it becomes the rule). A development-build scenario tag as a Visible()
filter was the alternative; a fresh process tests the real code path and
costs a few seconds per scenario.
